### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelBlockSurface.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class UVoxelWorldConfiguration;

/**
 * The walking surface of a block (cubic) world (world modes review WM-C5, KC6).
 *
 * A cubic block at voxel (i, j, k) is the cell [k * V, (k + 1) * V) above WorldOrigin, and the heightmap generators give
 * it the density of the column height H sampled at the cell's lower corner (i, j) (FInfinitePlaneWorldMode::
 * CalculateSignedDistance / SignedDistanceToDensity). The block is solid when that density reaches the surface threshold,
 * so the top face of the topmost solid block lies between H and H + V: the density isosurface that smooth meshing draws
 * (and that every surface query returned) is up to one block below the block tops a cubic world draws and collides with.
 * These helpers turn a generated column height into the block top the generator makes from it, exactly by the
 * generator's own density rule, and say where a position's block column is sampled.
 *
 * Smooth worlds and planets have no block surface (UsesBlockSurface is false there); cubic planets are out of scope.
 *
 * Thread safety: stateless and thread-safe (UsesBlockSurface reads a console variable).
 */
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelBlockSurface
{
	/**
	 * Whether a world's walking surface is block tops: cubic meshing in a heightmap world mode (InfinitePlane, IslandBowl),
	 * with voxel.Cubic.BlockSurface on (0 = the density isosurface, as before WM-C5).
	 *
	 * @param Config The world configuration
	 * @return True when surface queries and pads should use block tops
	 */
	static bool UsesBlockSurface(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * The lower corner, along one axis, of the block column containing a coordinate: where the generator samples the
	 * column's height (Origin + floor((Coord - Origin) / VoxelSize) * VoxelSize).
	 *
	 * @param Coord World coordinate (X or Y)
	 * @param Origin WorldOrigin's coordinate on the same axis
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @return The column's sample coordinate
	 */
	static double ColumnCorner(double Coord, double Origin, float VoxelSize);

	/**
	 * Whether the generator makes the voxel whose cell's lower face is at VoxelZ solid in a column of height Height (before
	 * caves): the same float arithmetic as the heightmap generators.
	 *
	 * @param Height The column's generated height (conditioning zones included)
	 * @param VoxelZ World Z of the voxel's cell bottom
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @return True when the voxel's density reaches the surface threshold
	 */
	static bool IsGeneratedSolid(float Height, double VoxelZ, float VoxelSize);

	/**
	 * The global voxel layer (above WorldOrigin) of the topmost voxel the generator makes solid in a column of height Height.
	 *
	 * @param Height The column's generated height
	 * @param OriginZ WorldOrigin.Z
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @return The voxel layer k; its block's top face is OriginZ + (k + 1) * VoxelSize
	 */
	static int64 TopSolidLayerForHeight(float Height, double OriginZ, float VoxelSize);

	/**
	 * The top face of the topmost block the generator makes solid in a column of height Height: the block-world surface for
	 * that height (between Height and Height + VoxelSize).
	 *
	 * @param Height The column's generated height
	 * @param OriginZ WorldOrigin.Z
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @return World Z of the block top
	 */
	static double BlockTopForHeight(float Height, double OriginZ, float VoxelSize);

	/**
	 * The top face of a voxel layer's blocks.
	 *
	 * @param Layer Global voxel layer above WorldOrigin
	 * @param OriginZ WorldOrigin.Z
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @return World Z of the layer's top face
	 */
	static double LayerTop(int64 Layer, double OriginZ, float VoxelSize)
	{
		return OriginZ + static_cast<double>(Layer + 1) * VoxelSize;
	}
};
```

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelCPUNoiseGenerator.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "IVoxelNoiseGenerator.h"
#include "VoxelBiomeDefinition.h"

class FInfinitePlaneWorldMode;
class FIslandBowlWorldMode;
class FSphericalPlanetWorldMode;
struct FSphericalPlanetParams;
class UVoxelCaveConfiguration;
struct FCaveLayerConfig;

/**
 * CPU-based noise generator for voxel terrain.
 *
 * Implements Perlin and Simplex 3D noise with fBm (Fractal Brownian Motion).
 * This is the fallback implementation for testing and editor scenarios.
 *
 * Performance: ~10-50ms per 32^3 chunk depending on octaves
 * Thread Safety: All methods are thread-safe
 *
 * @see IVoxelNoiseGenerator
 * @see FVoxelGPUNoiseGenerator
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator : public IVoxelNoiseGenerator
{
public:
	FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator();
	virtual ~FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator();

	// ==================== IVoxelNoiseGenerator Interface ====================

	virtual void Initialize() override;
	virtual void Shutdown() override;
	virtual bool IsInitialized() const override { return bIsInitialized; }

	virtual FVoxelGenerationHandle GenerateChunkAsync(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		FOnVoxelGenerationComplete OnComplete) override;

	virtual bool GenerateChunkCPU(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData) override;

	virtual float SampleNoiseAt(
		const FVector& WorldPosition,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params) override;

	virtual FRHIBuffer* GetGeneratedBuffer(const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle) override;

	virtual bool ReadbackToCPU(
		const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData) override;

	virtual void ReleaseHandle(const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle) override;

	// ==================== Noise Algorithms ====================

	/**
	 * Sample fBm (Fractal Brownian Motion) noise at a position: the noise every world mode's fields sample (terrain,
	 * continentalness, climate, caves, ores, the surface queries and the map). Since the world modes review's MP4 (WM-MP6,
	 * WM-MP7, decision D39; GenerationVersion 3) it is FVoxelPlanetNoise::FBM3D for heightmap worlds too: a hashed integer
	 * lattice with no period, split-origin sampling exact to float precision at any distance, and the continuous Simplex
	 * kernel (G43). The GPU's heightmap branch samples the same noise at a per-chunk origin (GenerateVoxelDensity.usf,
	 * PlanetNoise.ush), the two within float rounding of each other.
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample
	 * @param Params Noise parameters (octaves, frequency, etc.)
	 * @return Noise value in range approximately [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float FBM3D(const FVector& Position, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params);

	// The classic table noise (Ken Perlin's 256-entry permutation, the 0.6 Simplex kernel): what heightmap worlds sampled
	// before MP4. No generation path reads it; the tests keep it as the control that repeats every 256 lattice units and
	// steps across the simplex boundaries (Noise.PlanetHashNoPeriod, Noise.HeightmapNoise).

	/**
	 * Classic 3D Perlin noise (the permutation table; a 256-unit period).
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample
	 * @param Seed Random seed for permutation table
	 * @return Noise value in range [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float Perlin3D(const FVector& Position, int32 Seed = 0);

	/**
	 * Classic 3D Simplex noise (the permutation table, the 0.6 corner kernel).
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample
	 * @param Seed Random seed for permutation table
	 * @return Noise value in range [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float Simplex3D(const FVector& Position, int32 Seed = 0);

	/**
	 * Classic fBm over Perlin3D / Simplex3D / Cellular3D / Voronoi3D: what FBM3D was before MP4, for the tests' controls.
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample
	 * @param Params Noise parameters (octaves, frequency, etc.)
	 * @return Noise value in range approximately [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float ClassicFBM3D(const FVector& Position, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params);

	/**
	 * Classic 3D Cellular (Worley) noise at a position.
	 * Uses 3x3x3 cell search to find distances to nearest two feature points.
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample (pre-scaled by frequency)
	 * @param Seed Random seed
	 * @param OutF1 Distance to nearest feature point
	 * @param OutF2 Distance to second nearest feature point
	 */
	static void Cellular3D(const FVector& Position, int32 Seed, float& OutF1, float& OutF2);

	/**
	 * Classic 3D Voronoi noise at a position.
	 * Same as Cellular but also returns a stable cell ID.
	 *
	 * @param Position World position to sample (pre-scaled by frequency)
	 * @param Seed Random seed
	 * @param OutF1 Distance to nearest feature point
	 * @param OutF2 Distance to second nearest feature point
	 * @param OutCellID Stable hash-based cell identifier [0, 1]
	 */
	static void Voronoi3D(const FVector& Position, int32 Seed, float& OutF1, float& OutF2, float& OutCellID);

	/**
	 * Run the post-generation passes (water fill + underground classification) on already-generated
	 * voxel data. GenerateChunkCPU runs these inline; the GPU path runs shader ports of the same
	 * passes inside its generation graph (VoxelPostPasses.usf / AddVoxelPostPassDispatches), so this
	 * is the CPU reference implementation the shaders must stay bit-identical to (enforced by the
	 * GPUvsCPU parity tests). Static + state-free.
	 */
	static void ApplyPostReadbackPasses(const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request, TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

private:
	bool bIsInitialized = false;

	/** Counter for generating unique request IDs */
	std::atomic<uint64> NextRequestId{1};

	/** Stored results for async requests (CPU just completes immediately) */
	TMap<uint64, TArray<FVoxelData>> StoredResults;
	FCriticalSection ResultsLock;

	// ==================== World Mode Generation ====================

	/**
	 * Generate chunk using Infinite Plane world mode (2D heightmap).
	 */
	void GenerateChunkInfinitePlane(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		const FInfinitePlaneWorldMode& WorldMode,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	/**
	 * Generate chunk using full 3D noise (for volumetric modes).
	 */
	void GenerateChunk3DNoise(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	/**
	 * Generate chunk using Island Bowl world mode (bounded terrain with falloff).
	 */
	void GenerateChunkIslandBowl(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		const FIslandBowlWorldMode& WorldMode,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	/**
	 * Generate chunk using Spherical Planet world mode (radial terrain on sphere).
	 */
	void GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		const FSphericalPlanetWorldMode& WorldMode,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	// ==================== Noise Helper Functions ====================

	/** Fade function for smooth interpolation */
	static float Fade(float T);

	/** Linear interpolation */
	static float Lerp(float A, float B, float T);

	/** Gradient function for Perlin noise */
	static float Grad(int32 Hash, float X, float Y, float Z);

	/** Get permutation value with seed offset */
	static int32 Perm(int32 Index, int32 Seed = 0);

	/** Hash function for simplex noise */
	static int32 Hash(int32 I, int32 Seed = 0);

	/** Floor function that returns int32 */
	static int32 FastFloor(float X);

	/** Dot product for simplex gradient */
	static float SimplexDot(const int32* G, float X, float Y, float Z);

	// ==================== Cave Generation Helpers ====================

	/**
	 * Sample a single cave layer's carve density at a position.
	 * Cheese: single noise field threshold carving.
	 * Spaghetti/Noodle: dual-noise field intersection carving.
	 *
	 * @param WorldPos World position to sample
	 * @param LayerConfig Configuration for this cave layer
	 * @param WorldSeed Base world seed
	 * @param Planet On a planet, VerticalScale acts along local up (FSphericalPlanetWorldMode::ScaleAltitude, SP-B6);
	 *        null in heightmap modes, where it scales world Z
	 * @return Carve density in range [0, 1] where 0 = no carving, 1 = full carving
	 */
	static float SampleCaveLayer(const FVector& WorldPos, const FCaveLayerConfig& LayerConfig, int32 WorldSeed,
		const FSphericalPlanetParams* Planet = nullptr);

public:
	/**
	 * Calculate total cave carve density at a position from all enabled layers.
	 * Applies depth constraints, biome scaling, and union composition (max).
	 *
	 * Public + static + state-free so FVoxelCaveQuery (the chunk-independent cave sampling facade)
	 * and any gameplay/AI caller can query cave presence without a loaded chunk. Keep bit-identical
	 * to the generation-time carving so the cave-presence heatmap matches real terrain.
	 *
	 * @param WorldPos World position to sample
	 * @param DepthBelowSurface Depth below terrain surface in voxels
	 * @param BiomeID Current biome ID for per-biome overrides
	 * @param CaveConfig Cave configuration data asset
	 * @param WorldSeed Base world seed
	 * @param bIsUnderwater The terrain surface above is under the water (caves keep UnderwaterMinDepth below it)
	 * @param Planet On a planet, the layers' VerticalScale acts along local up (SP-B6); null in heightmap modes
	 * @return Carve density in range [0, 1]
	 */
	static float CalculateCaveDensity(
		const FVector& WorldPos,
		float DepthBelowSurface,
		uint8 BiomeID,
		const UVoxelCaveConfiguration* CaveConfig,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		bool bIsUnderwater = false,
		const FSphericalPlanetParams* Planet = nullptr);

private:
	// ==================== Ore Vein Helpers ====================

	/**
	 * Sample ore vein noise at a position.
	 * @param WorldPos World position to sample
	 * @param OreConfig Configuration for this ore type
	 * @param WorldSeed Base world seed
	 * @return Normalized noise value in range [0, 1]
	 */
	static float SampleOreVeinNoise(const FVector& WorldPos, const struct FOreVeinConfig& OreConfig, int32 WorldSeed);

	/**
	 * Check if an ore vein should be placed at a position and return the ore material.
	 * @param WorldPos World position to check
	 * @param DepthBelowSurface Depth below terrain surface in voxels
	 * @param OreConfigs Array of ore configurations to check
	 * @param WorldSeed Base world seed
	 * @param OutMaterialID Output material ID if ore found
	 * @param PlanetRelativePos On a planet: the voxel's position relative to the planet centre; the Rarity test then
	 *        uses OreRarityHash (spherical SP-H3). Null: the heightmap modes' position hash, unchanged
	 * @return True if ore should be placed here
	 */
	static bool CheckOreVeinPlacement(
		const FVector& WorldPos,
		float DepthBelowSurface,
		const TArray<struct FOreVeinConfig>& OreConfigs,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		uint8& OutMaterialID,
		const FVector* PlanetRelativePos = nullptr);

public:
	/**
	 * The integer key a planet's ore Rarity test hashes (spherical SP-H3): the voxel's planet-relative position rounded
	 * to whole uu (floor(x + 0.5) per axis). Exact on the CPU (double) and the GPU (float holds whole uu below 2^24, a
	 * 167 km radius), and the same at every LOD for the same world position.
	 *
	 * @param PlanetRelativePos Position relative to the planet centre
	 * @return The key
	 */
	static FIntVector OreRarityKey(const FVector& PlanetRelativePos);

	/**
	 * A planet's ore vein noise (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP5): the same 2-octave field at the ore's frequency and seed,
	 * by the planet noise (FVoxelPlanetNoise) at the planet-relative position, a streak squashed along one direction per
	 * ore type (GetPlanetOreStreakDirection). Exact at any radius; the planet's ores move with it.
	 *
	 * @param PlanetRelativePos Position relative to the planet centre
	 * @param OreConfig Ore vein configuration
	 * @param WorldSeed World seed
	 * @return Noise in [0, 1]
	 */
	static float SamplePlanetOreVeinNoise(const FVector& PlanetRelativePos, const struct FOreVeinConfig& OreConfig, int32 WorldSeed);

	/** A planet streak ore's direction: the heightmap formula at the origin (one per ore type, WM-BP5). */
	static FVector GetPlanetOreStreakDirection(const struct FOreVeinConfig& OreConfig);

	/** Where a planet ore samples its noise: the planet-relative position, squashed along the streak direction for a streak. */
	static FVector GetPlanetOreSamplePoint(const FVector& PlanetRelativePos, const struct FOreVeinConfig& OreConfig);

	/**
	 * A planet's ore Rarity value in [0, 1) (spherical SP-H3): an integer hash of the key and the seed, the same bits on
	 * the CPU and the GPU (GpuOreRarityHash in BiomeMaterial.ush). Replaces frac(sin(p . k)), whose argument near 10^7
	 * the GPU's float and the CPU's double round differently. An ore is kept where the value is at most its Rarity.
	 *
	 * @param Key OreRarityKey of the voxel
	 * @param Seed World seed
	 * @return Value in [0, 1), 24 bits
	 */
	static float OreRarityHash(const FIntVector& Key, int32 Seed);

private:

	// ==================== Water Fill Pass ====================

	/** Post-generation: mark air voxels below water level as water via column scan. */
	static void ApplyWaterFillPass(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	/**
	 * ApplyWaterFillPass on a planet (SP-B8): the sea is the sphere of WaterRadius around the planet centre, and the
	 * open-sea seeding runs along lines in local down instead of world-Z columns. Same phases and barriers.
	 */
	static void ApplyRadialWaterFillPass(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

	/** Post-generation: mark air voxels below terrain surface as underground (caves, enclosed voids). */
	static void ApplyUndergroundClassificationPass(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);
};

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelCaveQuery.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class UVoxelCaveConfiguration;

/**
 * Stateless, thread-safe cave queries against the procedural generator.
 *
 * The cave-layer sibling of FVoxelSurfaceQuery: answers "how carved is world position P" by
 * re-running the CPU generator's cave-carving math (FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::CalculateCaveDensity),
 * decoupled from chunk streaming so it works for any region whether or not a chunk is loaded.
 *
 * Deterministic for a given (cave config, seed). Safe to call off the game thread. Used by the
 * editor field-visualization tools (cave-presence heatmap) and available to gameplay/AI that
 * needs "is there a cave here" without a resident chunk.
 *
 * @see FVoxelSurfaceQuery
 * @see FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::CalculateCaveDensity
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelCaveQuery
{
public:
	/**
	 * Cave carve density [0,1] at an explicit world position. 0 = solid (no carving),
	 * 1 = fully carved (open cave).
	 *
	 * Mirrors generation-time carving exactly (FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::GenerateChunkInfinitePlane):
	 * depth below the surface is measured in voxels, and only positions strictly BELOW the terrain
	 * surface carve — at or above the surface this returns 0 (there is no solid terrain to carve).
	 *
	 * @param WorldPos      World position to sample.
	 * @param SurfaceHeight Terrain surface Z at WorldPos.XY (e.g. FVoxelSurfaceQuery::GetSurfaceHeight).
	 * @param VoxelSize     World units per voxel (depth below surface is measured in voxels).
	 * @param BiomeID       Surface biome ID for per-biome cave overrides; 0 if unknown.
	 * @param CaveConfig    Cave configuration; null => returns 0.
	 * @param WorldSeed     World seed.
	 * @param bIsUnderwater Whether the surface column is submerged (suppresses caves per config).
	 * @return Carve density in [0,1].
	 */
	static float SampleCaveDensityAt(
		const FVector& WorldPos,
		float SurfaceHeight,
		float VoxelSize,
		uint8 BiomeID,
		const UVoxelCaveConfiguration* CaveConfig,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		bool bIsUnderwater = false);
};

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelGPUNoiseGenerator.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "IVoxelNoiseGenerator.h"
#include "RHIFwd.h"

// Forward declarations to avoid heavy RDG includes in header
class FRDGPooledBuffer;
class FRHIGPUBufferReadback;

/**
 * Result of polling a non-blocking GPU generation readback.
 * Pending = compute/readback still in flight; Ready = OutVoxelData filled; Failed = handle invalid/error.
 */
enum class EVoxelGPUReadbackStatus : uint8
{
	Pending,
	Ready,
	Failed
};

/**
 * GPU-based noise generator for voxel terrain.
 *
 * Uses compute shaders to generate voxel density data on the GPU.
 * This is the high-performance implementation for runtime terrain generation.
 *
 * Performance: ~0.1-1ms per 32^3 chunk on modern GPUs
 * Thread Safety: Must be called from render thread or with proper synchronization
 *
 * @see IVoxelNoiseGenerator
 * @see FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelGPUNoiseGenerator : public IVoxelNoiseGenerator
{
public:
	FVoxelGPUNoiseGenerator();
	virtual ~FVoxelGPUNoiseGenerator();

	// ==================== IVoxelNoiseGenerator Interface ====================

	virtual void Initialize() override;
	virtual void Shutdown() override;
	virtual bool IsInitialized() const override { return bIsInitialized; }

	virtual FVoxelGenerationHandle GenerateChunkAsync(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		FOnVoxelGenerationComplete OnComplete) override;

	virtual bool GenerateChunkCPU(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData) override;

	virtual float SampleNoiseAt(
		const FVector& WorldPosition,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params) override;

	virtual FRHIBuffer* GetGeneratedBuffer(const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle) override;

	virtual bool ReadbackToCPU(
		const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData) override;

	virtual void ReleaseHandle(const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle) override;

	// ==================== Non-blocking streaming API ====================
	// Poll-based GPU generation for the chunk-manager streaming path. Unlike the delegate-based
	// GenerateChunkAsync + blocking ReadbackToCPU (test/editor use), this dispatches the compute pass
	// and an FRHIGPUBufferReadback copy, then hands ownership of readiness to the caller who polls
	// each frame — no thread is ever stalled (option (a) integration model).

	/**
	 * Dispatch density generation for a chunk on the GPU and enqueue an async readback.
	 * Non-blocking: returns immediately with a handle to poll via PollGenerateChunkGPU.
	 *
	 * @param Request Generation request parameters
	 * @return Handle for polling the readback (RequestId != 0 on success)
	 */
	FVoxelGenerationHandle BeginGenerateChunkGPU(const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request);

	/**
	 * Poll a pending GPU generation started with BeginGenerateChunkGPU.
	 * Call once per frame on the game thread until it returns Ready or Failed.
	 *
	 * @param Handle Handle from BeginGenerateChunkGPU
	 * @param OutVoxelData Filled with unpacked voxel data when the status is Ready
	 * @return Pending (still in flight), Ready (OutVoxelData filled), or Failed (invalid handle/error)
	 */
	EVoxelGPUReadbackStatus PollGenerateChunkGPU(const FVoxelGenerationHandle& Handle, TArray<FVoxelData>& OutVoxelData);

private:
	bool bIsInitialized = false;

	/** Counter for generating unique request IDs */
	std::atomic<uint64> NextRequestId{1};

	/** Stored generation results */
	struct FGenerationResult
	{
		TRefCountPtr<FRDGPooledBuffer> OutputBuffer;
		TRefCountPtr<FRDGPooledBuffer> StagingBuffer;
		int32 ChunkSize = 0;
		bool bReadbackComplete = false;
		TArray<FVoxelData> CachedData;

		// ---- Non-blocking streaming readback (BeginGenerateChunkGPU / PollGenerateChunkGPU) ----
		/** Async GPU→CPU readback for the density buffer; owned here, deleted after the Lock completes. */
		FRHIGPUBufferReadback* DensityReadback = nullptr;
		/** Total voxel count (ChunkSize^3) — cached so the poll knows the readback byte size. */
		int32 TotalVoxels = 0;
		/** Set true on the render thread AFTER EnqueueCopy is recorded — guards IsReady() polling. */
		std::atomic<bool> bReadbackEnqueued{false};
		/** Set true on the render thread once CachedData has been filled from the mapped readback. */
		std::atomic<bool> bDataReady{false};
		/** Game-thread-only: true once the Lock render command has been enqueued (avoids double-enqueue). */
		bool bLockInFlight = false;

		FGenerationResult() = default;

		/**
		 * Safety net for an abandoned readback. The normal completion path (the Lock render command
		 * enqueued by PollGenerateChunkGPU) deletes + nulls DensityReadback itself. If a handle is
		 * released while that command is still in flight, the command's captured TSharedPtr keeps
		 * this result alive and this destructor then runs on the render thread after it completes —
		 * so ReleaseHandle needs no FlushRenderingCommands. Shutdown still flushes before dropping
		 * all references at once.
		 */
		~FGenerationResult()
		{
			if (DensityReadback)
			{
				delete DensityReadback;
				DensityReadback = nullptr;
			}
		}
	};

	TMap<uint64, TSharedPtr<FGenerationResult>> GenerationResults;
	FCriticalSection ResultsLock;

	/** Dispatch the compute shader on the render thread */
	void DispatchComputeShader(
		const FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request,
		uint64 RequestId,
		TSharedPtr<FGenerationResult> Result,
		FOnVoxelGenerationComplete OnComplete);

	/** Create the structured buffer for output */
	FBufferRHIRef CreateOutputBuffer(int32 ChunkSize);

	/** Create a staging buffer for CPU readback */
	FBufferRHIRef CreateStagingBuffer(int32 ChunkSize);
};
```

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelGeneration.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "Modules/ModuleManager.h"

DECLARE_LOG_CATEGORY_EXTERN(LogVoxelGeneration, Log, All);

/**
 * VoxelGeneration module - GPU and CPU noise generation for VoxelWorlds.
 *
 * Provides compute shader-based terrain generation using Perlin and Simplex noise
 * with CPU fallback for testing and editor scenarios.
 *
 * Dependencies: VoxelCore, RenderCore, RHI
 *
 * @see IVoxelNoiseGenerator
 * @see Documentation/ARCHITECTURE.md
 */
class FVoxelGenerationModule : public IModuleInterface
{
public:
	/** IModuleInterface implementation */
	virtual void StartupModule() override;
	virtual void ShutdownModule() override;

	/**
	 * Singleton-like access to this module's interface.
	 */
	static inline FVoxelGenerationModule& Get()
	{
		return FModuleManager::LoadModuleChecked<FVoxelGenerationModule>("VoxelGeneration");
	}

	/**
	 * Checks if this module is loaded and ready.
	 */
	static inline bool IsAvailable()
	{
		return FModuleManager::Get().IsModuleLoaded("VoxelGeneration");
	}
};

// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "VoxelCoreTypes.h"
#include "VoxelTerrainConditioning.h"
#include "IslandBowlWorldMode.h"
#include "SphericalPlanetWorldMode.h"
#include "VoxelNoiseTypes.generated.h"

class UVoxelBiomeConfiguration;
class UVoxelCaveConfiguration;

// Re-export EVoxelNoiseType and FVoxelNoiseParams from VoxelCoreTypes.h
// These are defined in VoxelCore to avoid circular dependencies with VoxelWorldConfiguration

/**
 * Request for generating voxel data for a chunk.
 */
USTRUCT(BlueprintType)
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

	/** Chunk coordinate in chunk space */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Request")
	FIntVector ChunkCoord = FIntVector::ZeroValue;

	/** LOD level for this chunk (0 = highest detail) */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Request")
	int32 LODLevel = 0;

	/** Number of voxels per chunk edge */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Request")
	int32 ChunkSize = 32;

	/** Size of each voxel in world units */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Request")
	float VoxelSize = 100.0f;

	/** Noise parameters for generation */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Request")
	FVoxelNoiseParams NoiseParams;

	// ==================== World Mode Parameters ====================

	/** World generation mode */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "World Mode")
	EWorldMode WorldMode = EWorldMode::InfinitePlane;

	/** Sea level height for terrain generation (world units) */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "World Mode")
	float SeaLevel = 0.0f;

	/** Scale factor for noise-to-height conversion */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "World Mode")
	float HeightScale = 5000.0f;

	/** Base height offset from sea level */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "World Mode")
	float BaseHeight = 0.0f;

	// ==================== Biome Parameters ====================

	/** Whether to enable biome-based material selection */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Biome")
	bool bEnableBiomes = true;

	/**
	 * Biome configuration containing biome definitions, blending parameters,
	 * and height material rules. Set by VoxelChunkManager from the world config.
	 * Not a UPROPERTY - kept alive by VoxelWorldConfiguration.
	 */
	UVoxelBiomeConfiguration* BiomeConfiguration = nullptr;

	// ==================== World Origin ====================

	/** World origin offset - all chunk positions are relative to this */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "World Mode")
	FVector WorldOrigin = FVector::ZeroVector;

	// ==================== Island Mode Parameters ====================

	/**
	 * Island mode configuration (used when WorldMode == IslandBowl). Built by FVoxelWorldModeFactory, so the
	 * centre is absolute (WorldOrigin + the config's offset), the same as every other island consumer.
	 */
	FIslandBowlParams IslandParams;

	// ==================== Spherical Planet Mode Parameters ====================

	/** Spherical planet configuration (used when WorldMode == SphericalPlanet). Built by FVoxelWorldModeFactory */
	FSphericalPlanetParams SphericalPlanetParams;

	// ==================== Cave Parameters ====================

	/** Whether cave generation is enabled for this request */
	bool bEnableCaves = false;

	/**
	 * Cave configuration containing layer definitions and biome overrides.
	 * Set by VoxelChunkManager from the world config.
	 * Not a UPROPERTY - kept alive by VoxelWorldConfiguration.
	 */
	UVoxelCaveConfiguration* CaveConfiguration = nullptr;

	// ==================== Water Level Parameters ====================

	/** Whether water level is enabled for this request */
	bool bEnableWaterLevel = false;

	/** Water level height for InfinitePlane/IslandBowl modes (world units) */
	float WaterLevel = 0.0f;

	/**
	 * Water radius for SphericalPlanet mode (world units from planet center). Double (WM-BP4): it meets R-sized values;
	 * generation compares the sea as the altitude WaterRadius - PlanetRadius, formed in double.
	 */
	double WaterRadius = 0.0;

	// ==================== Terrain Conditioning (Phase 6c) ====================

	/**
	 * Terrain conditioning zones overlapping this chunk — gen-time height flattening under POIs /
	 * claims. Gathered (game thread) by VoxelChunkManager when the request is built; applied by the
	 * heightmap generator. Empty for most chunks (no per-chunk cost when there's no conditioning).
	 */
	UPROPERTY()
	TArray<FVoxelConditioningZone> ConditioningZones;

	FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest() = default;

	/** Get the world position of this chunk's origin (includes WorldOrigin offset) */
	FVector GetChunkWorldPosition() const
	{
		// All chunks cover the same world area regardless of LOD level
		// LOD only affects voxel resolution within the chunk, not chunk position
		float ChunkWorldSize = ChunkSize * VoxelSize;
		return WorldOrigin + FVector(ChunkCoord) * ChunkWorldSize;
	}

	/** Get the effective voxel size at this LOD level */
	float GetEffectiveVoxelSize() const
	{
		return VoxelSize * FMath::Pow(2.0f, static_cast<float>(LODLevel));
	}
};

/**
 * Handle for tracking async generation operations.
 */
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelGenerationHandle
{
	/** Unique identifier for this generation request */
	uint64 RequestId = 0;

	/** Whether generation has completed */
	bool bIsComplete = false;

	/** Whether generation succeeded */
	bool bWasSuccessful = false;

	/** Error message if generation failed */
	FString ErrorMessage;

	FVoxelGenerationHandle() = default;
	explicit FVoxelGenerationHandle(uint64 InRequestId) : RequestId(InRequestId) {}

	bool IsValid() const { return RequestId != 0; }
	bool IsComplete() const { return bIsComplete; }
	bool WasSuccessful() const { return bIsComplete && bWasSuccessful; }
};

/** Delegate called when async generation completes */
DECLARE_DELEGATE_TwoParams(FOnVoxelGenerationComplete, FVoxelGenerationHandle /*Handle*/, bool /*bSuccess*/);

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelPlanetNoise.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "VoxelCoreTypes.h"

/**
 * A noise-space point split for precision (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP5): the integer lattice cell holding it and the
 * fraction within that cell. For Simplex the split is in the skewed lattice; for Perlin, Cellular and Voronoi in the
 * cube lattice. The cell wraps mod 2^32 (the lattice hash reads only its 32 bits), so any double position splits.
 */
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelNoiseSplit
{
	/** Lattice cell (wrapping). */
	FIntVector Cell = FIntVector::ZeroValue;

	/** Fraction within the cell, in [0, 1) on each axis. */
	FVector3f Frac = FVector3f::ZeroVector;
};

/**
 * The terrain noise (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP5, decision D22; every world mode since the world modes review's MP4, decision
 * D39): the noise every field samples (terrain, continentalness, temperature, moisture, caves and ores), on the CPU and, bit
 * for bit in its algebra, on the GPU (PlanetNoise.ush). The name is from spherical Phase 6, when planets alone had it;
 * FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::FBM3D, the heightmap entry point, has come through here since MP4 (GenerationVersion 3).
 *
 * Two things differ from the classic table noise heightmap worlds sampled before MP4 (FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::ClassicFBM3D):
 *
 * - A hashed integer lattice (LatticeHash, the ore Rarity hash's mixing) instead of Ken Perlin's 256-entry permutation
 *   table, so the noise has no period: the old table repeated every field every 256 lattice units, a 1,000 km planet's
 *   terrain 61 times around its equator.
 * - Split-origin sampling: a sample point is an origin, split in double into an integer lattice cell and a float fraction
 *   per octave (Split), plus a small float offset in noise units. Every float operation sees only values of the size of
 *   a cell, so the noise is exact to float precision at any distance from the centre (a float position at 1e8 uu is 8 uu
 *   coarse: 10 uu terraces in the terrain's top octave on Review_Planet_L). The CPU splits each sample at the point
 *   itself (FBM3D(Position)); the GPU splits a per-chunk origin on the CPU and adds each voxel's offset (FBM3D(Origin,
 *   Offset) is that form on the CPU, for parity and tests).
 *
 * - A continuous Simplex kernel (G43, PlanetGenerationVersion 6): the classic (0.6 - d^2)^4 corner weight stepped where
 *   a sample crossed into the next simplex (up to 136 uu along Review_Planet_L's cube face edges, where every octave's
 *   boundary lies); it is now that weight less its value and slope at d^2 = 0.5. voxel.Noise.ContinuousSimplex 0
 *   restores the classic one (A/B; voxel.Planet.ContinuousSimplex before MP4).
 *
 * The octave loop (frequencies multiplied in float, amplitudes, normalisation) is FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::FBM3D's.
 *
 * Thread safety: stateless, any thread.
 * @see WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md §20.1 (WM-BP5, D22), Shaders/Private/PlanetNoise.ush
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelPlanetNoise
{
public:
	/** Most octaves a field has (FVoxelNoiseParams::Octaves' ClampMax). */
	static constexpr int32 MaxOctaves = 16;

	/**
	 * The lattice hash: a 32-bit value from a lattice corner and a seed, with wrapping multiplies, xors and shifts only
	 * (the mixing of FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::OreRarityHash), mirrored by PlanetLatticeHash in PlanetNoise.ush.
	 *
	 * @param X Corner X (wrapping)
	 * @param Y Corner Y
	 * @param Z Corner Z
	 * @param Seed The field's seed
	 * @return The hash
	 */
	static uint32 LatticeHash(uint32 X, uint32 Y, uint32 Z, int32 Seed)
	{
		uint32 H = X * 0x8DA6B343u;
		H ^= Y * 0xD8163841u;
		H ^= Z * 0xCB1AB31Fu;
		H ^= static_cast<uint32>(Seed) * 0x9E3779B9u;
		H ^= H >> 16;
		H *= 0x7FEB352Du;
		H ^= H >> 15;
		H *= 0x846CA68Bu;
		H ^= H >> 16;
		return H;
	}

	/**
	 * Split a noise-space point (a position already multiplied by the octave's frequency) into its lattice cell and
	 * fraction, in double: in the skewed lattice for Simplex, the cube lattice otherwise.
	 *
	 * @param NoisePoint The point in noise units
	 * @param Type Noise type
	 * @return The split
	 */
	static FVoxelNoiseSplit Split(const FVector& NoisePoint, EVoxelNoiseType Type);

	/**
	 * One octave of noise at Origin + Offset.
	 *
	 * @param Origin The split origin
	 * @param Offset The sample's offset from the origin in noise units (unskewed; small: a few cells for float precision)
	 * @param Type Noise type (Cellular: F1 mapped to [-1, 1]; Voronoi: F2 - F1 mapped to [-1, 1], as the heightmap FBM)
	 * @param Seed The field's seed
	 * @return Noise in about [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float Sample(const FVoxelNoiseSplit& Origin, const FVector3f& Offset, EVoxelNoiseType Type, int32 Seed);

	/** Simplex noise at Origin + Offset (Origin split in the skewed lattice): about [-1, 1], continuous across simplices. */
	static float Simplex(const FVoxelNoiseSplit& Origin, const FVector3f& Offset, int32 Seed);

	/**
	 * voxel.Noise.ContinuousSimplex: whether Simplex uses the continuous corner kernel (G43, the default) or the classic one.
	 *
	 * @return True for the continuous kernel
	 */
	static bool IsContinuousSimplex();

	/** Perlin (improved gradient) noise at Origin + Offset: about [-1, 1]. */
	static float Perlin(const FVoxelNoiseSplit& Origin, const FVector3f& Offset, int32 Seed);

	/**
	 * Cellular (Worley) noise at Origin + Offset: the distances to the nearest two feature points over the 3x3x3 cells
	 * around the sample, one feature point per cell from the hash.
	 *
	 * @param OutF1 Nearest distance
	 * @param OutF2 Second nearest distance
	 * @param OutCellID Optional: a [0, 1) value per nearest cell (Voronoi)
	 */
	static void Cellular(const FVoxelNoiseSplit& Origin, const FVector3f& Offset, int32 Seed, float& OutF1, float& OutF2, float* OutCellID = nullptr);

	/**
	 * Each octave's frequency as the FBM loop computes it: Frequency, then multiplied by Lacunarity in float per octave.
	 *
	 * @param Params Noise parameters
	 * @param OutFrequencies MaxOctaves floats
	 * @return The number of octaves (Params.Octaves clamped to [1, MaxOctaves])
	 */
	static int32 OctaveFrequencies(const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params, float* OutFrequencies);

	/**
	 * fBm at a position, each octave split at the point itself (the CPU planet paths: generation, the surface function,
	 * the surface queries, the map).
	 *
	 * @param Position Sample position in uu, relative to the planet centre (double)
	 * @param Params Noise parameters
	 * @return Noise in about [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float FBM3D(const FVector& Position, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params);

	/**
	 * fBm at Origin + Offset: Origin split per octave (SplitOctaves), Offset scaled by each octave's frequency in float.
	 * The GPU's form (PlanetFBM3D), on the CPU for parity and tests.
	 *
	 * @param Origin Origin in uu (double)
	 * @param Offset The sample's offset from Origin in uu (float; within a chunk or so)
	 * @param Params Noise parameters
	 * @return Noise in about [-1, 1]
	 */
	static float FBM3D(const FVector& Origin, const FVector3f& Offset, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params);

	/**
	 * The per-octave splits of an origin, what the GPU generator uploads for a chunk (2 float4s each).
	 *
	 * @param Origin Origin in uu (double)
	 * @param Params Noise parameters (type, frequency, lacunarity, octaves)
	 * @param OutSplits MaxOctaves splits
	 * @return The number of octaves written
	 */
	static int32 SplitOctaves(const FVector& Origin, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params, FVoxelNoiseSplit* OutSplits);

	/**
	 * The 2-octave Simplex field the planet's continentalness, temperature and moisture use (the heightmap modes' climate
	 * parameters).
	 *
	 * @param Seed The field's seed
	 * @param Frequency The field's frequency
	 * @return Noise parameters
	 */
	static FVoxelNoiseParams MakeFieldParams(int32 Seed, float Frequency);

	// ==================== Double reference (tests) ====================

	/** One octave with the same lattice and hash, every step in double (Noise.SplitOrigin's reference). */
	static double ReferenceSample(const FVector& NoisePoint, EVoxelNoiseType Type, int32 Seed);

	/** fBm with ReferenceSample, the frequencies as OctaveFrequencies gives them. */
	static double ReferenceFBM3D(const FVector& Position, const FVoxelNoiseParams& Params);
};
```

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelSurfaceQuery.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "VoxelData.h"

struct FVoxelBiomeSnapshot;
struct FVoxelNoiseParams;
struct FVoxelSeaSurface;
class IVoxelWorldMode;
class FSphericalPlanetWorldMode;

/**
 * A sampled terrain surface point: from the procedural generator (FVoxelSurfaceQuery, no loaded chunk data required) or
 * from loaded, edit-merged voxels (UVoxelChunkManager::QueryEditMergedSurfacePoint).
 */
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelSurfaceSample
{
	/**
	 * Heightmap modes: world-space Z of the terrain surface at the queried X,Y. On a planet, which has no Z per (X, Y):
	 * the surface's altitude above the datum (as Altitude).
	 */
	float Height = 0.0f;

	/** Surface normal derived from the height-field gradient (points up-ish). */
	FVector Normal = FVector::UpVector;

	/** Slope angle in degrees (0 = flat, 90 = vertical), measured against Up. */
	float SlopeDegrees = 0.0f;

	/** World position of the surface point (heightmap modes: (X, Y, Height)); spherical SP-A3. */
	FVector Position = FVector::ZeroVector;

	/** Local up at the point: +Z in heightmap modes, the radial direction on a planet. */
	FVector Up = FVector::UpVector;

	/** The point's altitude above the datum (IVoxelWorldMode::GetAltitude). */
	float Altitude = 0.0f;

	/** Surface material ID (biome-blended; 0 when no biome config). */
	uint8 MaterialID = 0;

	/** Dominant biome ID (0 when no biome config). */
	uint8 BiomeID = 0;
};

/**
 * A surface point's material mix (G45, FVoxelSurfaceQuery::QueryPlanetSurfaceMaterialMixAt): its two leading surface
 * materials and the second's share of them, what the per-voxel material picks there cover on average.
 */
struct FVoxelSurfaceMaterialMix
{
	/** The leading material, then the second (the leading one again when there is no second) */
	uint8 Materials[2] = { 0, 0 };

	/** The second material's share of the two, in [0, 0.5] */
	float Weight = 0.0f;

	/** The dominant biome */
	uint8 BiomeID = 0;
};

/**
 * Stateless, thread-safe surface queries against the procedural generator.
 *
 * Answers "what is the terrain surface at world X,Y" (height, normal, slope, biome,
 * material) by re-sampling IVoxelWorldMode + the biome noise pipeline — decoupled
 * from chunk streaming, so it works for any region whether or not a chunk is loaded.
 *
 * This is the shared core reused by:
 * - FVoxelTreeInjector (deterministic tree placement)
 * - VoxelPCG's Voxel Surface Sampler node (PCG point generation)
 *
 * All math here is pure and deterministic for a given (world mode, noise params,
 * seed, biome config). Safe to call off the game thread.
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelSurfaceQuery
{
public:
	/** Terrain surface Z at a world X,Y. Thin wrapper over IVoxelWorldMode::GetTerrainHeightAt. */
	static float GetSurfaceHeight(
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float WorldX, float WorldY,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams);

	/**
	 * Slope angle (degrees) at a world X,Y, from a central-difference height gradient.
	 * VoxelSize is used as the sampling step.
	 */
	static float ComputeSlopeDegrees(
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float WorldX, float WorldY, float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams);

	/**
	 * Surface normal at a world X,Y, from a central-difference height gradient.
	 * Returns a normalized up-facing vector (FVector(-dHdX, -dHdY, 1) normalized).
	 */
	static FVector ComputeSurfaceNormal(
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float WorldX, float WorldY, float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams);

	/**
	 * Query surface material and biome at a world position.
	 * Uses the SAME biome pipeline as the CPU noise generator (temperature/moisture/continentalness
	 * noise -> tiered biome blend -> blended surface material -> height rules), via the shared
	 * FVoxelBiomeSnapshot algorithm cores.
	 *
	 * Takes a value snapshot instead of the UVoxelBiomeConfiguration UObject: build it once per
	 * batch with FVoxelBiomeSnapshot::FromConfig (game thread), then call this freely from any
	 * thread — including tasks that may outlive the world.
	 *
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data (FVoxelBiomeSnapshot::FromConfig)
	 * @param OutSurfaceMaterial Surface material ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 * @param OutBiomeID Dominant biome ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 */
	static void QuerySurfaceConditions(
		float WorldX, float WorldY, float TerrainHeight, float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel,
		uint8& OutSurfaceMaterial, uint8& OutBiomeID);

	/**
	 * Convenience: sample everything (height, normal, slope, material, biome) at a world X,Y.
	 * Computes the height gradient once and derives both slope and normal from it.
	 * BiomeSnapshot as in QuerySurfaceConditions — hoist one per batch via FromConfig.
	 *
	 * @param Zones Optional heightmap conditioning zones there (POI pads and their falloff rings; gather them for the place,
	 *              e.g. UVoxelChunkManager::GatherConditioningZones): the generated surface, as the generator layers them
	 *              onto the natural height (FVoxelTerrainConditioning::ApplyToHeight), for the height, the gradient and the
	 *              material's water and height rules (world modes review G23). Planet zones are ignored. Null or empty:
	 *              the natural surface.
	 */
	static FVoxelSurfaceSample SampleSurface(
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float WorldX, float WorldY, float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel,
		const TArray<struct FVoxelConditioningZone>* Zones = nullptr);

	/**
	 * Material and biome on a planet as GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet writes them for a voxel at a position, before caves
	 * and ores (spherical SP-A3): temperature, moisture and continentalness at the direction's point on the datum sphere,
	 * the biome blend, the blended material at the position's depth below the terrain (with the sea's variant when water
	 * is on), height rules by its altitude. Pass a surface point for the surface material (depth 0).
	 *
	 * @param Planet The planet world mode
	 * @param Position A surface point, or any position (its depth below the terrain along its direction is used)
	 * @param VoxelSize Voxel size (generation measures the depth in voxels)
	 * @param NoiseParams Terrain noise (the radial height; its seed derives the climate seeds)
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data (FVoxelBiomeSnapshot::FromConfig)
	 * @param Sea The world's sea (FVoxelSeaSurface::FromConfig): a sphere on a planet
	 * @param OutSurfaceMaterial Surface material ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 * @param OutBiomeID Dominant biome ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 * @param Zones Optional planet conditioning zones there (spherical SP-B10): the terrain's radius is the conditioned one,
	 *              as generation's, so a pad's surface point reads the surface material at depth 0
	 */
	static void QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions(
		const FSphericalPlanetWorldMode& Planet,
		const FVector& Position,
		float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		const FVoxelSeaSurface& Sea,
		uint8& OutSurfaceMaterial, uint8& OutBiomeID,
		const TArray<struct FVoxelConditioningZone>* Zones = nullptr);

	/**
	 * QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions from a terrain altitude the caller has already sampled (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP9: the
	 * far field samples the altitude of every patch vertex once and reads the material from it). The same arithmetic:
	 * QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions calls this after its own SampleRadialDisplacement.
	 *
	 * @param Planet The planet world mode
	 * @param Direction Unit direction from the planet centre
	 * @param TerrainAltitude The terrain's altitude along Direction (conditioned where zones apply)
	 * @param Continentalness The continentalness SampleRadialDisplacement returned for Direction (the biome blend reuses it)
	 * @param VoxelAltitude The queried point's altitude (TerrainAltitude for the surface material: depth 0)
	 * @param VoxelSize Voxel size (generation measures the depth in voxels)
	 * @param NoiseParams Terrain noise (its seed derives the climate seeds)
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data
	 * @param Sea The world's sea
	 * @param OutSurfaceMaterial Surface material ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 * @param OutBiomeID Dominant biome ID (0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 */
	static void QueryPlanetSurfaceConditionsAt(
		const FSphericalPlanetWorldMode& Planet,
		const FVector& Direction,
		float TerrainAltitude,
		float Continentalness,
		double VoxelAltitude,
		float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		const FVoxelSeaSurface& Sea,
		uint8& OutSurfaceMaterial, uint8& OutBiomeID);

	/**
	 * The surface material mix at a planet's surface point (G45): what QueryPlanetSurfaceConditionsAt's per-voxel picks cover
	 * there on average, for the far field, whose vertices lie km apart while a blend zone's picks change every few voxels.
	 * The blend's materials and shares at depth 0 (FVoxelBiomeSnapshot::GetBlendedMaterialShares, the sea's variant below it),
	 * height rules applied to each, summed per material; the two largest, with the second's share of the two.
	 *
	 * @param Planet The planet world mode
	 * @param Direction Unit direction from the planet centre
	 * @param TerrainAltitude The terrain's altitude along Direction (conditioned where zones apply)
	 * @param Continentalness The continentalness SampleRadialDisplacement returned for Direction
	 * @param NoiseParams Terrain noise (its seed derives the climate seeds)
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data
	 * @param Sea The world's sea
	 * @return The mix (material 0 and weight 0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 */
	static FVoxelSurfaceMaterialMix QueryPlanetSurfaceMaterialMixAt(
		const FSphericalPlanetWorldMode& Planet,
		const FVector& Direction,
		float TerrainAltitude,
		float Continentalness,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		const FVoxelSeaSurface& Sea);

	/**
	 * The surface material mix at a heightmap world's surface point (world modes review WM-MP1, the heightmap far field):
	 * what QuerySurfaceConditions's per-voxel picks cover there on average. The climate and blend as QuerySurfaceConditions
	 * samples them, the blend's materials and shares at depth 0 (the sea's variant under WaterLevel), height rules applied
	 * to each, summed per material; the two largest, with the second's share of the two.
	 *
	 * @param WorldX World X
	 * @param WorldY World Y
	 * @param TerrainHeight The generated surface height there (conditioning zones included)
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data
	 * @param WorldSeed The terrain noise's seed (the climate seeds derive from it)
	 * @param bEnableWaterLevel Whether the world has a sea
	 * @param WaterLevel The sea's level (world Z)
	 * @return The mix (material 0 and weight 0 when the snapshot is invalid)
	 */
	static FVoxelSurfaceMaterialMix QuerySurfaceMaterialMix(
		float WorldX, float WorldY, float TerrainHeight,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		int32 WorldSeed,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel);

	/**
	 * Everything at the analytic surface on the local up-line through a position, in any world mode (spherical SP-A3):
	 * heightmap modes return SampleSurface at (X, Y) with Position (X, Y, Height); a planet the surface along the
	 * direction from its centre (GetSurfacePoint), the slope against local up, and QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions.
	 *
	 * @param WorldMode World mode
	 * @param WorldPos Any position on the up-line
	 * @param VoxelSize Voxel size (the heightmap gradient's step)
	 * @param NoiseParams Terrain noise
	 * @param BiomeSnapshot Value-captured biome data
	 * @param Sea The world's sea (FVoxelSeaSurface::FromConfig): the WaterLevel plane, or a planet's sphere
	 * @param Zones Optional conditioning zones there: the generated surface and its conditions. On a planet its zones
	 *              (spherical SP-B10, GetConditionedSurfacePoint); in heightmap modes its zones (SampleSurface's, G23)
	 * @return The surface sample
	 */
	static FVoxelSurfaceSample SampleSurfacePoint(
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		const FVector& WorldPos, float VoxelSize,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const FVoxelBiomeSnapshot& BiomeSnapshot,
		const FVoxelSeaSurface& Sea,
		const TArray<struct FVoxelConditioningZone>* Zones = nullptr);

	/**
	 * Find the topmost terrain surface in a vertical voxel column (index 0 = lowest Z, ascending).
	 *
	 * This is the near-band, EDIT-AWARE path: the caller assembles a column of edit-merged voxels
	 * (so digging/building is honored) and this finds the exact surface. Scans from the top for the
	 * highest solid voxel with air directly above, interpolates the density crossing at
	 * VOXEL_SURFACE_THRESHOLD, and reads the surface voxel's material/biome. Pure and deterministic.
	 *
	 * @param ColumnLowToHigh Voxels ordered from lowest to highest world Z
	 * @param BaseZ           World Z of ColumnLowToHigh[0]
	 * @param VoxelSize       World units per voxel (column step)
	 * @return false if the column has no air-over-solid transition (caller falls back to the generator)
	 */
	static bool ExtractSurfaceFromColumn(
		const TArray<FVoxelData>& ColumnLowToHigh,
		float BaseZ, float VoxelSize,
		float& OutHeight, uint8& OutMaterialID, uint8& OutBiomeID);
};
```

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelTerrainConditioning.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "VoxelTerrainConditioning.generated.h"

/**
 * A terrain conditioning zone — blends the generated terrain height toward a target within a
 * footprint, with a smooth falloff ring back to the natural terrain.
 *
 * Generation-time and deterministic: the base terrain IS flat here, consistent everywhere as
 * chunks stream, with no edit storage. Produced by IVoxelTerrainConditioner (game-side, e.g. from
 * POI claims) and applied by the generator before the SDF/density is derived. Pure data —
 * safe to copy onto a generation request and read on background generation threads.
 *
 * Two kinds (spherical SP-B10, decision D15 in WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md §19.1):
 *  - A heightmap zone (Direction zero): an XY disc around Center, TargetHeight a world Z; the
 *    heightmap generators blend the column height (ApplyToHeight).
 *  - A planet zone (Direction set, IsRadial): a cap on the planet's datum sphere around Direction,
 *    InnerRadius and FalloffWidth measured along the surface (great-circle distance at the planet
 *    radius), TargetHeight an altitude above the datum; the planet generators blend the terrain's
 *    altitude along each direction (ApplyToAltitude), so a pad is level in gravity. Center is unused.
 * Each kind is ignored by the other's functions, so a zone of the wrong kind contributes nothing.
 *
 * See WorldClaims/Documentation/CLAIMS_ARCHITECTURE.md "Terrain conditioning".
 */
USTRUCT(BlueprintType)
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelConditioningZone
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

	/** Footprint center (world X,Y). */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning")
	FVector2D Center = FVector2D::ZeroVector;

	/** Radius (world units) fully blended to TargetHeight. */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning")
	float InnerRadius = 1000.0f;

	/** Width (world units) of the falloff ring outside InnerRadius, easing back to natural terrain. */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning")
	float FalloffWidth = 1000.0f;

	/** World Z the terrain is blended toward inside the footprint (a planet zone: the altitude above the datum). */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning")
	float TargetHeight = 0.0f;

	/** Overall strength [0,1]: 1 = fully reach TargetHeight at the center, 0 = no effect. */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning", meta = (ClampMin = "0.0", ClampMax = "1.0"))
	float Strength = 1.0f;

	/**
	 * Planet zones only: the unit direction from the planet centre to the zone's centre (MakeRadial). Zero (the
	 * default) makes a heightmap zone, which uses Center.
	 */
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Conditioning")
	FVector Direction = FVector::ZeroVector;

	FVoxelConditioningZone() = default;

	FVoxelConditioningZone(const FVector2D& InCenter, float InInnerRadius, float InFalloffWidth, float InTargetHeight, float InStrength = 1.0f)
		: Center(InCenter), InnerRadius(InInnerRadius), FalloffWidth(InFalloffWidth), TargetHeight(InTargetHeight), Strength(InStrength)
	{
	}

	/**
	 * A planet zone (spherical SP-B10): a cap on the datum sphere.
	 *
	 * @param InDirection Direction from the planet centre to the zone's centre (normalized here)
	 * @param InInnerRadius Fully blended radius, along the surface (uu)
	 * @param InFalloffWidth Falloff ring width, along the surface (uu)
	 * @param InTargetAltitude Altitude above the datum the terrain is blended toward
	 * @param InStrength Overall strength [0, 1]
	 * @return The zone
	 */
	static FVoxelConditioningZone MakeRadial(const FVector& InDirection, float InInnerRadius, float InFalloffWidth,
		float InTargetAltitude, float InStrength = 1.0f)
	{
		FVoxelConditioningZone Zone(FVector2D::ZeroVector, InInnerRadius, InFalloffWidth, InTargetAltitude, InStrength);
		Zone.Direction = InDirection.GetSafeNormal();
		return Zone;
	}

	/** Whether this is a planet zone (a direction is set). */
	bool IsRadial() const { return !Direction.IsNearlyZero(); }

	/**
	 * The great-circle distance between two unit directions on a sphere: R * atan2(|A x B|, A . B), well conditioned at
	 * small angles (unlike acos), in float on the GPU too.
	 *
	 * @param A Unit direction
	 * @param B Unit direction
	 * @param Radius Sphere radius
	 * @return Distance along the sphere's surface
	 */
	static double GreatCircleDistance(const FVector& A, const FVector& B, double Radius)
	{
		return Radius * FMath::Atan2(FVector::CrossProduct(A, B).Size(), FVector::DotProduct(A, B));
	}

	/**
	 * A planet zone's weight along a direction: GetWeightAt's profile over the great-circle distance from the zone's
	 * centre on the datum sphere.
	 *
	 * @param InDirection Unit direction from the planet centre
	 * @param PlanetRadius The datum radius
	 * @return The weight (0 for a heightmap zone)
	 */
	float GetWeightAtDirection(const FVector& InDirection, double PlanetRadius) const
	{
		return IsRadial() ? GetWeightAtDistance(GreatCircleDistance(InDirection, Direction, PlanetRadius)) : 0.0f;
	}

	/** A planet zone's influence as an angle from its direction: (InnerRadius + FalloffWidth) / PlanetRadius. */
	double GetAngularRadius(double PlanetRadius) const
	{
		return (static_cast<double>(InnerRadius) + FMath::Max(0.0, static_cast<double>(FalloffWidth))) / FMath::Max(PlanetRadius, 1.0);
	}

	/**
	 * Whether a planet zone's influence reaches a cap (a direction and a half-angle): the angle between their centres is
	 * at most the cap's angle plus the zone's angular radius.
	 *
	 * @param CapDirection Unit direction of the cap's centre
	 * @param CapAngle The cap's half-angle (radians; pi or more covers the sphere)
	 * @param PlanetRadius The datum radius
	 * @return False for a heightmap zone
	 */
	bool MeetsCap(const FVector& CapDirection, double CapAngle, double PlanetRadius) const
	{
		if (!IsRadial())
		{
			return false;
		}
		const double Angle = FMath::Atan2(FVector::CrossProduct(CapDirection, Direction).Size(), FVector::DotProduct(CapDirection, Direction));
		return Angle <= CapAngle + GetAngularRadius(PlanetRadius);
	}

	/** Conditioning weight at (X,Y): Strength inside InnerRadius, smoothstep to 0 across FalloffWidth, 0 beyond. */
	float GetWeightAt(double X, double Y) const
	{
		const double Dx = X - Center.X;
		const double Dy = Y - Center.Y;
		return GetWeightAtDistance(FMath::Sqrt(Dx * Dx + Dy * Dy));
	}

	/** The weight at a distance from the centre: Strength inside InnerRadius, smoothstep to 0 across FalloffWidth, 0 beyond. */
	float GetWeightAtDistance(double Dist) const
	{
		if (Dist <= InnerRadius)
		{
			return Strength;
		}
		const double Falloff = FMath::Max(1.0, static_cast<double>(FalloffWidth));
		if (Dist >= static_cast<double>(InnerRadius) + Falloff)
		{
			return 0.0f;
		}
		const double T = (Dist - InnerRadius) / Falloff;        // 0 at inner edge, 1 at outer edge
		const double S = 1.0 - (T * T * (3.0 - 2.0 * T));       // smoothstep 1 -> 0
		return static_cast<float>(Strength * S);
	}

	/** XY world-space bounds of the zone's influence (center +/- (InnerRadius + FalloffWidth)). */
	FBox2D GetBounds2D() const
	{
		const float R = InnerRadius + FMath::Max(0.0f, FalloffWidth);
		return FBox2D(Center - FVector2D(R, R), Center + FVector2D(R, R));
	}
};

/**
 * Boundary-safe interface for supplying terrain conditioning zones at generation time.
 *
 * Implemented game-side (e.g. from POI / construction claims). VoxelWorlds stays POI-agnostic — it
 * only asks "what conditioning applies to this region?". Implementations must be pure and
 * thread-safe: the chunk manager queries them while building generation requests.
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API IVoxelTerrainConditioner
{
public:
	virtual ~IVoxelTerrainConditioner() = default;

	/**
	 * Append conditioning zones overlapping the given world-space XY region.
	 * @param Region    Chunk (or query) XY bounds.
	 * @param OutZones  Append overlapping zones here.
	 */
	virtual void GatherConditioning(const FBox2D& Region, TArray<FVoxelConditioningZone>& OutZones) const = 0;

	/**
	 * Planets (spherical SP-B10): append the planet zones (FVoxelConditioningZone::MakeRadial) whose influence reaches a
	 * cap on the sphere. The default supplies none, so a heightmap-only conditioner conditions nothing on a planet.
	 * @param Direction     Unit direction from the planet centre to the cap's centre
	 * @param AngularRadius The cap's half-angle in radians (a chunk's, or a query's; pi or more is the whole sphere)
	 * @param OutZones      Append overlapping zones here
	 */
	virtual void GatherConditioningOnSphere(const FVector& Direction, double AngularRadius, TArray<FVoxelConditioningZone>& OutZones) const
	{
	}
};

/**
 * Stateless helper for applying conditioning zones to a generated terrain height.
 */
struct FVoxelTerrainConditioning
{
	/**
	 * Blend BaseHeight toward each zone's TargetHeight by the zone's weight at (X,Y). Zones layer in
	 * order (a later zone blends on top of earlier ones). Returns the conditioned height. Planet zones are skipped.
	 */
	static float ApplyToHeight(double X, double Y, float BaseHeight, const TArray<FVoxelConditioningZone>& Zones)
	{
		float H = BaseHeight;
		for (const FVoxelConditioningZone& Zone : Zones)
		{
			if (Zone.IsRadial())
			{
				continue;
			}
			const float W = Zone.GetWeightAt(X, Y);
			if (W > 0.0f)
			{
				H = FMath::Lerp(H, Zone.TargetHeight, W);
			}
		}
		return H;
	}

	/**
	 * Planets (spherical SP-B10): blend the terrain's altitude along a direction toward each planet zone's TargetHeight
	 * (an altitude) by its weight there, layered in order like ApplyToHeight; heightmap zones are skipped. The planet
	 * generators (CPU and GPU) and every reader of the generated planet surface apply it to the radial displacement.
	 *
	 * @param Direction Unit direction from the planet centre
	 * @param PlanetRadius The datum radius (zone distances are measured on it)
	 * @param BaseAltitude The natural terrain's altitude along Direction
	 * @param Zones Zones (planet zones apply)
	 * @return The conditioned altitude
	 */
	static float ApplyToAltitude(const FVector& Direction, double PlanetRadius, float BaseAltitude, const TArray<FVoxelConditioningZone>& Zones)
	{
		float A = BaseAltitude;
		for (const FVoxelConditioningZone& Zone : Zones)
		{
			const float W = Zone.GetWeightAtDirection(Direction, PlanetRadius);
			if (W > 0.0f)
			{
				A = FMath::Lerp(A, Zone.TargetHeight, W);
			}
		}
		return A;
	}
};
```

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelTreeInjector.h

// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "VoxelData.h"
#include "VoxelTreeTypes.h"

struct FVoxelNoiseParams;
class IVoxelWorldMode;
class UVoxelBiomeConfiguration;

/**
 * One voxel tree as the injector places it (world modes review WM-C8, KC9): recomputed from the same seeded positions the
 * stamp uses, so gameplay can find and fell the tree whose voxels a chunk holds.
 */
struct FVoxelTreeInstance
{
	/** Global voxel coordinate of the trunk's lowest block (the ground's top voxel, which the trunk replaces). */
	FIntVector BaseVoxel = FIntVector::ZeroValue;

	/** Index into the templates the trees were placed with. */
	int32 TemplateIndex = INDEX_NONE;

	/** The tree's own seed (height and canopy variation). */
	uint32 Seed = 0;

	bool IsValid() const { return TemplateIndex != INDEX_NONE; }
};

/** One voxel a tree's stamp writes (FVoxelTreeInjector::CollectTreeVoxels). */
struct FVoxelTreeVoxel
{
	/** Global voxel coordinate (above WorldOrigin, in voxels). */
	FIntVector GlobalVoxel = FIntVector::ZeroValue;

	/** The material the stamp writes there (the template's trunk or leaf material). */
	uint8 MaterialID = 0;

	/** A trunk block (written over anything) rather than a leaf (written only over air or other trees' blocks). */
	bool bTrunk = false;
};

/**
 * Stamps voxel tree blocks into chunk VoxelData during generation.
 *
 * Deterministic: same seed + templates = same trees every time.
 * Cross-chunk safe: trees near chunk borders are computed by checking
 * neighboring chunk tree positions and only writing voxels within bounds.
 *
 * Thread Safety: All methods are stateless and thread-safe.
 *
 * @see FVoxelTreeTemplate
 */
class VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelTreeInjector
{
public:
	/**
	 * Inject all trees that affect a given chunk.
	 *
	 * Computes tree positions for this chunk AND neighboring chunks (within tree extent range),
	 * then stamps tree blocks only within this chunk's voxel bounds.
	 * Tree positions are filtered by per-template placement rules (material, biome, slope, elevation).
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord This chunk's coordinate
	 * @param ChunkSize Voxels per chunk edge
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @param WorldOrigin World origin offset
	 * @param WorldSeed World generation seed
	 * @param Templates Available tree templates
	 * @param NoiseParams Noise parameters for height sampling
	 * @param WorldMode World mode interface for height queries
	 * @param TreeDensity Trees per chunk (fractional = probability)
	 * @param BiomeConfig Biome configuration for material/biome queries (can be nullptr to skip biome filtering)
	 * @param bEnableWaterLevel Whether water level is active
	 * @param WaterLevel Water level height (trees below this are skipped)
	 * @param InOutVoxelData Voxel data to modify (must be ChunkSize^3 elements)
	 */
	static void InjectTrees(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		int32 ChunkSize, float VoxelSize,
		const FVector& WorldOrigin, int32 WorldSeed,
		const TArray<FVoxelTreeTemplate>& Templates,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float TreeDensity,
		const UVoxelBiomeConfiguration* BiomeConfig,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& InOutVoxelData);

	/**
	 * Compute deterministic tree positions for a specific source chunk.
	 * Positions are filtered by per-template placement rules.
	 *
	 * @param SourceChunkCoord The chunk to compute tree positions for
	 * @param ChunkSize Voxels per chunk edge
	 * @param VoxelSize World units per voxel
	 * @param WorldOrigin World origin offset
	 * @param WorldSeed World generation seed
	 * @param NoiseParams Noise parameters for height sampling
	 * @param WorldMode World mode interface for height queries
	 * @param TreeDensity Trees per chunk
	 * @param Templates Available templates (for random selection)
	 * @param BiomeConfig Biome configuration for material/biome queries (can be nullptr)
	 * @param bEnableWaterLevel Whether water level filtering is active
	 * @param WaterLevel Water level height
	 * @param OutGlobalVoxelPositions Global voxel coordinates of tree base positions
	 * @param OutTemplateIDs Template ID for each tree
	 * @param OutSeeds Per-tree random seed
	 */
	static void ComputeTreePositionsForChunk(
		const FIntVector& SourceChunkCoord,
		int32 ChunkSize, float VoxelSize,
		const FVector& WorldOrigin, int32 WorldSeed,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float TreeDensity,
		const TArray<FVoxelTreeTemplate>& Templates,
		const UVoxelBiomeConfiguration* BiomeConfig,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel,
		TArray<FIntVector>& OutGlobalVoxelPositions,
		TArray<int32>& OutTemplateIDs,
		TArray<uint32>& OutSeeds);

	/**
	 * Every voxel one tree's stamp writes, in the order the stamp writes them (canopy, then trunk), the trunk's base block
	 * included. The same shape enumeration as InjectTrees, so the result equals what the stamp wrote wherever nothing
	 * stamped later (a neighbouring tree, or terrain under a leaf) overrode it.
	 *
	 * @param BaseGlobalVoxel The tree's base (FVoxelTreeInstance::BaseVoxel)
	 * @param Template The tree's template
	 * @param TreeSeed The tree's seed
	 * @param OutVoxels Receives the voxels (appended)
	 */
	static void CollectTreeVoxels(const FIntVector& BaseGlobalVoxel, const FVoxelTreeTemplate& Template, uint32 TreeSeed,
		TArray<FVoxelTreeVoxel>& OutVoxels);

	/**
	 * The trees whose trunk passes through a voxel (world modes review WM-C8): recomputed from the seeded positions of the
	 * chunks around it, as InjectTrees places them. A tree the stamp skipped (its base under an overhang) is still listed;
	 * callers check the voxels are there. Arguments as InjectTrees.
	 *
	 * @param GlobalVoxel The voxel (global voxel coordinate)
	 * @param OutTrees Receives the trees (appended); usually one, two only where trunks touch
	 */
	static void FindTreesWithTrunkAt(
		const FIntVector& GlobalVoxel,
		int32 ChunkSize, float VoxelSize,
		const FVector& WorldOrigin, int32 WorldSeed,
		const TArray<FVoxelTreeTemplate>& Templates,
		const FVoxelNoiseParams& NoiseParams,
		const IVoxelWorldMode& WorldMode,
		float TreeDensity,
		const UVoxelBiomeConfiguration* BiomeConfig,
		bool bEnableWaterLevel, float WaterLevel,
		TArray<FVoxelTreeInstance>& OutTrees);

private:
	/**
	 * Visit every voxel a tree's stamp writes, canopy first then trunk (the trunk punches through the canopy): the shape
	 * StampTree writes and CollectTreeVoxels lists.
	 */
	static void ForEachTreeVoxel(const FIntVector& BaseGlobalVoxel, const FVoxelTreeTemplate& Template, uint32 TreeSeed,
		TFunctionRef<void(int32 GX, int32 GY, int32 GZ, uint8 MaterialID, bool bTrunk)> Visit);

	/**
	 * Stamp a single tree, writing only voxels that fall within the target chunk bounds.
	 */
	static void StampTree(
		const FIntVector& BaseGlobalVoxel,
		const FVoxelTreeTemplate& Template,
		uint32 TreeSeed,
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		int32 ChunkSize,
		TArray<FVoxelData>& InOutVoxelData);

	/** Compute a deterministic seed for a chunk's trees */
	static uint32 ComputeTreeChunkSeed(const FIntVector& ChunkCoord, int32 WorldSeed);

	/** LCG random in [0,1) */
	static float RandomFromSeed(uint32& Seed);

	/** LCG random integer in [Min, Max] */
	static int32 RandomIntFromSeed(uint32& Seed, int32 Min, int32 Max);

	// Surface slope and biome/material queries are provided by the shared
	// FVoxelSurfaceQuery utility (VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelSurfaceQuery.h),
	// reused by both this injector and the VoxelPCG surface sampler.
};

### Source/VoxelGeneration/Public/VoxelWorldModeFactory.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "IVoxelWorldMode.h"
#include "IslandBowlWorldMode.h"
#include "SphericalPlanetWorldMode.h"

class UVoxelWorldConfiguration;
struct FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest;

/**
 * The one place world-mode parameters are built from a world configuration (world modes review WM-A1, KI3/KI4;
 * spherical requirement SP-A6).
 *
 * Generation (CPU and GPU, through the request), the LOD strategy's island and shell culls, the chunk manager's
 * analytic world mode, the map and the editor field viewer all take their params from here, so they cannot drift
 * apart again. Before this, island params were copied field by field in six places and the island centre meant two
 * things: generation read IslandCenterX/Y as an absolute position, the LOD cull as an offset from WorldOrigin.
 *
 * Positions in the built params are absolute world space: the island centre is WorldOrigin + IslandCenterX/Y (the
 * config's documented meaning), the planet centre is WorldOrigin.
 *
 * Thread safety: the functions read the configuration, so call them on the game thread (or wherever the config is
 * not being edited). The world modes they return are immutable afterwards and safe to share with worker threads.
 */
struct VOXELGENERATION_API FVoxelWorldModeFactory
{
	/**
	 * Version of the generation code, recorded in every world save's fingerprint (WM-A4). Bump it when the same
	 * configuration starts generating different terrain (noise, height composition, island falloff, caves, ...): saves
	 * made before the bump are then refused, instead of loading their edits and records onto terrain that moved.
	 * 1: the first recorded version (WM-A1 moved islands whose WorldOrigin is not zero onto WorldOrigin + offset).
	 * 2: G18, the GPU heightmap caves apply the cave configuration's biome overrides and underwater minimum depth as the
	 *    CPU does (GPU InfinitePlane and IslandBowl worlds stop carving caves under the sea and in biomes scaled to 0).
	 * 3: world modes review MP4 (WM-MP6, WM-MP7, decision D39): heightmap worlds sample the planet's noise
	 *    (FVoxelPlanetNoise: a hashed lattice with no 256-unit period, split-origin sampling, the continuous Simplex
	 *    kernel) in every field, and their ores take the planet's streak map and Rarity hash; every heightmap world's
	 *    terrain changes once. A planet's terrain does not change, but this version is in every fingerprint, so planet
	 *    saves from before are refused too.
	 */
	static constexpr int32 GenerationVersion = 3;

	/**
	 * Version of the planet's generation, in a planet's fingerprint shape ("PlanetGeneration=N") so a change to planet
	 * terrain refuses planet saves only; GenerationVersion would refuse every save. 2: spherical Phase 1 (noise by 3D
	 * direction on the datum sphere, continentalness on the radial height, materials by altitude; SP-B1, SP-B2, SP-B5).
	 * 3: spherical Phase 4 (decision D13): the ore Rarity test hashes the planet-relative position (SP-H3), and the
	 * planet's map tiles, explored tiles, map overlays and surface NPC ids key on the surface coordinate.
	 * 4: spherical Phase 5 (decision D16): planet generation applies conditioning zones (POI pads, SP-B10), and POIs,
	 * their claims, campsites and dungeons are placed on planets (dungeon records keyed by cube-sphere cell).
	 * 5: spherical Phase 6 (decisions D21, D22): the planet noise (FVoxelPlanetNoise: a hashed lattice with no period,
	 * split-origin sampling) for every planet field, caves and ores relative to the planet centre, and the SDF in double.
	 * 6: G43 (decision D27): the planet Simplex noise's corner kernel is continuous at the simplex boundaries, so every
	 * planet field (terrain, continentalness, climate, caves, ores) moves slightly and the steps along the cube sphere's
	 * face edges are gone.
	 * Fingerprints from before have no entry and are refused.
	 */
	static constexpr int32 PlanetGenerationVersion = 6;

	/**
	 * Terrain params for the heightmap modes (InfinitePlane, IslandBowl).
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration
	 * @return SeaLevel, HeightScale and BaseHeight from the config
	 */
	static FWorldModeTerrainParams MakeTerrainParams(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * Terrain params for a spherical planet: radial, so SeaLevel is 0 and the height scale is PlanetHeightScale.
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration
	 * @return The planet's terrain params
	 */
	static FWorldModeTerrainParams MakePlanetTerrainParams(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * Island params, with the centre resolved to WorldOrigin + IslandCenterX/Y.
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration (read whatever its WorldMode)
	 * @return The island's shape, extent, falloff, absolute centre and edge height
	 */
	static FIslandBowlParams MakeIslandParams(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * Spherical planet params; the planet is centred on WorldOrigin.
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration (read whatever its WorldMode)
	 * @return The planet's radius, shell and centre
	 */
	static FSphericalPlanetParams MakePlanetParams(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * The analytic world mode for a configuration, with its biome context set (continentalness), so its height
	 * queries match generation. Each caller gets its own instance: a caller whose background tasks may outlive the
	 * chunk manager (map tiles, POI placement) must not borrow the manager's.
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration
	 * @return A new world mode of the config's WorldMode (InfinitePlane for an unknown mode)
	 */
	static TSharedRef<IVoxelWorldMode> Create(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config);

	/**
	 * Fill a generation request's world-mode fields: WorldMode, WorldOrigin, the terrain params (the planet's for a
	 * planet) and the island or planet params. Leaves every other field alone.
	 *
	 * @param Config World configuration
	 * @param Request Generation request to fill
	 */
	static void FillGenerationRequest(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config, FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest& Request);

	/**
	 * The world's fingerprint for saves (WM-A4, KI7; SP-G9): the world mode, the mode's shape params (island: shape,
	 * radius, size Y for a rectangle, falloff width and curve, centre, edge height; planet: radius, shell, centre), the
	 * voxel grid (voxel size, chunk size, world origin: edits are stored per chunk) and GenerationVersion. Terrain
