### Source/VoxelLOD/Public/DistanceBandLODStrategy.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "IVoxelLODStrategy.h"
#include "LODTypes.h"
#include "VoxelCoreTypes.h"
#include "VoxelCubeSphere.h"
#include "VoxelWorldModeTypes.h"

class IVoxelWorldMode;
class FSphericalPlanetWorldMode;

/**
 * Distance-based LOD strategy using concentric rings.
 *
 * The default LOD implementation. Uses configurable distance bands
 * around the viewer to determine LOD levels. Simple, predictable,
 * and efficient for most use cases.
 *
 * Features:
 * - Configurable distance bands with LOD levels
 * - Optional LOD morphing for smooth transitions
 * - Optional view frustum culling
 * - Priority boost for chunks in view direction
 *
 * Performance: O(n) for visible chunk enumeration where n = chunks in range
 * Memory: Minimal state (just configuration)
 *
 * @see IVoxelLODStrategy
 * @see Documentation/LOD_SYSTEM.md
 */
class VOXELLOD_API FDistanceBandLODStrategy : public IVoxelLODStrategy
{
public:
	FDistanceBandLODStrategy();
	virtual ~FDistanceBandLODStrategy() = default;

	// ==================== IVoxelLODStrategy Interface ====================

	virtual int32 GetLODForChunk(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	/** With LOD on, GetLODForChunk; with it off, the raw band for the chunk's distance. */
	virtual int32 GetDistanceBandLOD(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual float GetLODMorphFactor(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual TArray<FChunkLODRequest> GetVisibleChunks(
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual void GetChunksToLoad(
		TArray<FChunkLODRequest>& OutLoad,
		const TSet<FIntVector>& LoadedChunks,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual void GetChunksToUnload(
		TArray<FIntVector>& OutUnload,
		const TSet<FIntVector>& LoadedChunks,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual void Initialize(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration* WorldConfig) override;

	virtual void Update(const FLODQueryContext& Context, float DeltaTime) override;

	virtual float GetChunkPriority(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	virtual FString GetDebugInfo() const override;

	virtual void DrawDebugVisualization(
		UWorld* World,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const override;

	// ==================== Configuration ====================

	/** Get the configured LOD bands */
	const TArray<FLODBand>& GetLODBands() const { return LODBands; }

	/** Set LOD bands configuration. The next Update rebuilds the balanced LOD cache. */
	void SetLODBands(const TArray<FLODBand>& InBands);

	/** Enable/disable LOD morphing */
	void SetMorphingEnabled(bool bEnabled) { bEnableMorphing = bEnabled; }
	bool IsMorphingEnabled() const { return bEnableMorphing; }

	/** Enable/disable view frustum culling */
	void SetFrustumCullingEnabled(bool bEnabled) { bEnableFrustumCulling = bEnabled; }
	bool IsFrustumCullingEnabled() const { return bEnableFrustumCulling; }

	/** Set the unload distance multiplier (chunks beyond MaxDistance * multiplier are unloaded) */
	void SetUnloadDistanceMultiplier(float Multiplier) { UnloadDistanceMultiplier = Multiplier; }
	float GetUnloadDistanceMultiplier() const { return UnloadDistanceMultiplier; }

	/** Set the maximum view distance for chunk loading. The next Update rebuilds the balanced LOD cache. */
	void SetViewDistance(float Distance) { MaxViewDistance = Distance; bBalancedLODCacheDirty = true; }
	float GetViewDistance() const { return MaxViewDistance; }

	/**
	 * Viewer travel (uu) since the last balanced-LOD cache rebuild that triggers a rebuild by itself. Matches
	 * FVoxelLODEvalSchedule::MoveThreshold, the chunk manager's trigger for re-evaluating LOD levels, so the
	 * cache is never staler than the evaluation that reads it.
	 */
	static constexpr float BalancedLODCacheMoveThreshold = 100.0f;

	/** @return How many times the balanced LOD cache has been rebuilt (diagnostics and tests). */
	int32 GetBalancedLODCacheRebuildCount() const { return BalancedLODCacheRebuildCount; }

	/** Unload horizon: chunks beyond MaxViewDistance * UnloadDistanceMultiplier are out of range. */
	virtual float GetUnloadDistance() const override { return MaxViewDistance * UnloadDistanceMultiplier; }

	/** Load horizon: the configured view distance (chunks are requested within it). */
	virtual float GetLoadDistance() const override { return MaxViewDistance; }

	/**
	 * Horizontal distance in heightmap worlds (InfinitePlane, IslandBowl): the horizons are a cylinder, and each column's
	 * vertical extent is its window (GetColumnWindow), so the viewer's altitude never removes the ground (D8). On a
	 * planet the distance along the ground from the viewer's ground point (GetPlanetGroundDistance, spherical Phase 6,
	 * WM-BP8): the horizons are a cone around the viewer's up-line, and each chunk's radial extent is its window
	 * (IsInPlanetWindow), so a climbing viewer keeps its ground disk. LOD levels use 3D distance in every mode
	 * (GetDistanceToViewer).
	 */
	virtual float GetHorizonDistance(const FVector& ChunkCenter, const FVector& ViewerPosition) const override;

	/**
	 * The distance along the ground between a viewer and a point on a planet (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP8): the arc, on the
	 * sphere through the viewer's ground point, between the viewer's direction from the centre and the point's. A point
	 * straight above or below the viewer is at 0 whatever its altitude, as a heightmap world's horizontal distance is.
	 * @param Centre Planet centre
	 * @param GroundRadius Distance from the centre to the viewer's ground point (the terrain under the viewer)
	 * @param Viewer Viewer position
	 * @param Point Point (a chunk centre)
	 * @return GroundRadius times the angle between the two directions (uu)
	 */
	static double GetPlanetGroundDistance(const FVector& Centre, double GroundRadius, const FVector& Viewer, const FVector& Point);

	/**
	 * A planet viewer's ground point (WM-BP8): the analytic terrain along the viewer's direction from the centre, without
	 * conditioning zones (GetTerrainAltitude), at the radius GetPlanetGroundDistance measures on. Cached for the position
	 * the last Update saw; any other position is computed (one terrain sample). Game thread.
	 * @param ViewerPosition Viewer position
	 * @return Distance from the planet centre to the ground under the viewer (PlanetRadius on a heightmap world)
	 */
	double GetPlanetGroundRadius(const FVector& ViewerPosition) const;

	// ==================== The voxel cut-over (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP10, D18) ====================

	/**
	 * Whether the viewer is above the voxel cut-over (GetPlanetCutoverAltitude over the surface under it), so the window
	 * holds nothing and the far field alone draws the world. Decided in Update with hysteresis: suspended above the
	 * cut-over, resumed below CutoverResumeFraction of it. In every world mode only while the context reports a far field
	 * (FLODQueryContext::bFarFieldActive; world modes review WM-MP2, D38; planets too since G78: a suspended window with
	 * nothing to draw the world is a hole, whatever the mode).
	 */
	virtual bool IsWindowSuspended() const override { return bPlanetWindowSuspended; }

	/** The window resumes below this fraction of the cut-over altitude (hysteresis: a flyer hovering at it does not churn). */
	static constexpr double CutoverResumeFraction = 0.85;

	/**
	 * The default cut-over (PlanetVoxelCutoverAltitude 0) in view distances. At one, a 5,000 uu/s descent onto the 50 km
	 * test planet resumed the window 10 s before landing and touched down with half of it loaded (the far field drawing
	 * the rest; P6.5's benches, WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md §20.6); and a viewer 400 m up already saw only the far field.
	 */
	static constexpr double DefaultCutoverViewDistances = 3.0;

	/**
	 * Pure: the window's cut-over state after a viewer altitude.
	 * @param bWasSuspended The state before
	 * @param AltitudeOverSurface The viewer's altitude over the surface under it (the terrain, or the sea where higher)
	 * @param CutoverAltitude The cut-over altitude (<= 0: never suspended)
	 * @return Whether the window is suspended: above the cut-over, or still above CutoverResumeFraction of it once suspended
	 */
	static bool ComputeCutoverState(bool bWasSuspended, double AltitudeOverSurface, double CutoverAltitude);

	/**
	 * Pure: the cut-over state with the camera apart from the streaming viewer (the descent prefetch; G49,
	 * WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md §20.28). A suspended window resumes only with the viewer under CutoverResumeFraction of
	 * the cut-over and the camera under the cut-over itself: the prefetch's lead brings the resume forward to the cut-over
	 * at most, so a camera that stops above it never resumed the window, and one that stops under it keeps it (an active
	 * window suspends with the viewer above the cut-over, as before, and the viewer is never above the camera).
	 *
	 * @param bWasSuspended The state before
	 * @param AltitudeOverSurface The streaming viewer's altitude over the surface under it
	 * @param CutoverAltitude The cut-over altitude (<= 0: never suspended)
	 * @param CameraAltitudeOverSurface The camera's altitude over the same surface (the viewer's plus the lead)
	 * @return Whether the window is suspended
	 */
	static bool ComputeCutoverState(bool bWasSuspended, double AltitudeOverSurface, double CutoverAltitude, double CameraAltitudeOverSurface);

	/**
	 * Whether the last Update held a suspended window that the streaming viewer alone would have resumed: the viewer under
	 * the resume altitude by the prefetch's lead, the camera still over the cut-over (G49).
	 */
	bool IsCutoverResumeHeld() const { return bCutoverResumeHeld; }

	/**
	 * The cut-over altitude in force (uu over the surface; 0 = never): voxel.World.VoxelCutover when set (>= 0), else the
	 * configuration's PlanetVoxelCutoverAltitude, else DefaultCutoverViewDistances view distances. 0 on a heightmap world
	 * whose last Update saw no far field (WM-MP2).
	 */
	double GetPlanetCutoverAltitude() const;

	/** The viewer's altitude over the surface under it (the terrain, or the sea where higher), as the last Update saw it. */
	virtual double GetViewerSurfaceAltitude() const override { return ViewerSurfaceAltitude; }

	/**
	 * IVoxelLODStrategy: the cut-over in force, 0 while the last Update's context reported no far field (D38, every mode
	 * since G78); GetPlanetCutoverAltitude is the configured altitude whatever the far field.
	 */
	virtual double GetCutoverAltitude() const override { return bCutoverAllowed ? GetPlanetCutoverAltitude() : 0.0; }

	/** IVoxelLODStrategy: the far-field gate between Updates (the chunk manager, when the far field is built or released). */
	virtual void SetFarFieldActive(bool bActive) override { bCutoverAllowed = bActive; }

	/** The viewer's layer ± this many layers is streamed in columns near the viewer (heightmap worlds, D8). */
	static constexpr int32 NearWindowLayers = 2;

	/**
	 * Columns within this horizontal distance of the viewer add the viewer's layer ± NearWindowLayers to their surface
	 * slab: the first LOD band's outer edge plus two chunk widths (the margin keeps the extra layers from churning while
	 * the viewer wanders around the band edge). Within it they keep everything loaded in the height range, so a viewer
	 * moving up or down a layer unloads nothing nearby.
	 */
	float GetNearWindowRadius() const { return NearWindowRadius; }

	/**
	 * Planets: the near band's ceiling (IsInPlanetWindow's Load: the viewer's altitude ± NearWindowLayers near it; G52,
	 * WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md §20.7), as an altitude over the datum: the top of the surface slab over the near disk (the
	 * analytic surface's highest point within GetNearWindowRadius along the ground, margins included, + SlabSlackChunks),
	 * or the sea's surface + SlabSlackChunks where that is higher. A chunk off its slab wholly above it lies above its own
	 * slab too, so it holds air (edits are pinned by the chunk manager): the band reaches no higher, and a viewer above it
	 * takes none. A descending viewer used to stream a new layer of such chunks every second from 100 km up, and one on the
	 * ground kept a layer of them around it. A viewer inside or below the slab (caves, overhangs, a flyer near the ground)
	 * or at the sea's surface (a swimmer; the settle onto the sea waits for its chunk to cook) keeps the band below it.
	 * The shell's top without the slab, and on heightmap worlds, where the band is clipped to the terrain's height
	 * bounds. Game thread (memoized by the viewer's direction cell).
	 * @param ViewerPosition Viewer position
	 * @return Altitude over the datum (uu)
	 */
	double GetPlanetNearBandCeiling(const FVector& ViewerPosition) const;

	/**
	 * Planets: whether a viewer here takes the near band (its altitude over the datum is not above
	 * GetPlanetNearBandCeiling). The keep window does not change with it: what the band loaded stays within the unload
	 * distance.
	 * @param ViewerPosition Viewer position
	 * @return True when the near band streams around this viewer
	 */
	bool IsPlanetNearBandActive(const FVector& ViewerPosition) const;

	/**
	 * One column's vertical window, as absolute chunk layers (a range is empty when Min > Max). Heightmap worlds (D8):
	 * the column's surface slab (Slab*), plus the viewer's layer ± NearWindowLayers in a column near the viewer (Near*);
	 * both clipped to the terrain's height bounds. Planet (SP-C1): the column's crossings of the terrain shell
	 * (GetPlanetShellWindow), the one above the planet centre in Slab* and the one below in Near* (or one range when
	 * they meet); a planet streams by chunk, not by column (IsInPlanetWindow), and only enumerates candidates by
	 * crossings like these.
	 */
	struct FColumnWindow
	{
		int32 SlabMinZ = 0;
		int32 SlabMaxZ = -1;
		int32 NearMinZ = 0;
		int32 NearMaxZ = -1;

		bool Contains(int32 Z) const
		{
			return (Z >= SlabMinZ && Z <= SlabMaxZ) || (Z >= NearMinZ && Z <= NearMaxZ);
		}

		/** Calls Visit(Z) once for every layer in the window, slab first. */
		template <typename FVisit>
		void ForEachLayer(FVisit&& Visit) const
		{
			for (int32 Z = SlabMinZ; Z <= SlabMaxZ; ++Z)
			{
				Visit(Z);
			}
			for (int32 Z = NearMinZ; Z <= NearMaxZ; ++Z)
			{
				if (Z < SlabMinZ || Z > SlabMaxZ)
				{
					Visit(Z);
				}
			}
		}
	};

	/** Which window GetColumnWindow builds. */
	enum class EWindowUse : uint8
	{
		/** Chunks to stream in: the slab, plus the viewer's layer ± NearWindowLayers within GetNearWindowRadius. */
		Load,
		/**
		 * Chunks to keep (the unload rule, and the balanced-LOD cache's volume): the slab, plus the whole height range
		 * within GetNearWindowRadius. Wider than Load vertically, so nothing the near window loaded unloads when the
		 * viewer changes layer; the same radius, so the extra layers unload as soon as their column leaves it.
		 */
		Keep,
	};

protected:
	// ==================== Internal Helpers ====================

	/**
	 * Convert chunk coordinate to world-space center position.
	 */
	FVector ChunkCoordToWorldCenter(const FIntVector& ChunkCoord) const;

	/**
	 * Convert world position to chunk coordinate.
	 */
	FIntVector WorldPosToChunkCoord(const FVector& WorldPos) const;

	/**
	 * LOD distance from the viewer to a position: 3D in every world mode, so deep and high chunks fall into farther
	 * bands and compress (world modes review WM-S2; islands measured 2D until then, KI13). Whether a chunk is in range
	 * at all is GetHorizonDistance.
	 */
	float GetDistanceToViewer(
		const FVector& Position,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const;

	/** Whether the vertical window comes from the terrain (InfinitePlane, IslandBowl) rather than the viewer (planet). */
	bool IsHeightmapWorld() const { return WorldMode != EWorldMode::SphericalPlanet; }

	/**
	 * The vertical window of chunk column (ChunkX, ChunkY) for this viewer.
	 * @param ChunkX Column X, chunk coordinates
	 * @param ChunkY Column Y, chunk coordinates
	 * @param Context Query context (viewer position, world origin)
	 * @param Use Load (stream in) or Keep (retain)
	 * @return The column's window, absolute layers
	 */
	FColumnWindow GetColumnWindow(int32 ChunkX, int32 ChunkY, const FLODQueryContext& Context, EWindowUse Use) const;

	/**
	 * A planet column's crossing of the shell (SP-C1): the layers whose chunks meet the shell from ShellWindowInnerRadius
	 * to ShellWindowOuterRadius over the column's footprint. Exact for the footprint: its nearest and farthest points from
	 * the planet's axis bound the crossing, so it covers the shell at every latitude. Not clipped to the viewer's
	 * altitude any more (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP8: the viewer-Z clip lost the ground under a climbing viewer).
	 * @param ChunkX Column X, chunk coordinates
	 * @param ChunkY Column Y, chunk coordinates
	 * @param Context Query context (world origin)
	 * @param OutWindow Receives the crossings: above the centre in Slab*, below it in Near* (or one range in Slab*)
	 */
	void GetPlanetShellWindow(int32 ChunkX, int32 ChunkY, const FLODQueryContext& Context, FColumnWindow& OutWindow) const;

	/**
	 * A column of chunks along a grid axis, crossing a spherical shell around the planet centre: the layers along Axis
	 * whose chunks meet the shell [InnerRadius, OuterRadius] (touching counts). GetPlanetShellWindow is the Z axis with the
	 * window's radii; the planet's candidate enumeration runs along whichever axis is closest to the viewer's local up.
	 * @param Axis Column direction: 0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z
	 * @param ColumnA The column's chunk index along axis (Axis + 1) % 3
	 * @param ColumnB The column's chunk index along axis (Axis + 2) % 3
	 * @param InnerRadius Shell inner radius
	 * @param OuterRadius Shell outer radius
	 * @param WorldOrigin The chunk grid's origin
	 * @param OutWindow Receives the crossings: on the centre's positive side in Slab*, the negative in Near* (or one range)
	 */
	void GetShellCrossing(int32 Axis, int32 ColumnA, int32 ColumnB, double InnerRadius, double OuterRadius,
		const FVector& WorldOrigin, FColumnWindow& OutWindow) const;

	/**
	 * Whether a planet chunk is in the window for this viewer, apart from the horizon distance (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP8;
	 * the heightmap M4 rules on a sphere):
	 * - its radial extent meets the terrain shell (ShellWindowInnerRadius to ShellWindowOuterRadius, the terrain's real
	 *   bounds + ShellSlackChunks);
	 * - and its radial extent meets its slab (GetPlanetChunkSlab: the analytic surface's altitude range over the cap it
	 *   subtends ± SlabSlackChunks; with slab culling off, the whole shell);
	 * - or, within GetNearWindowRadius of the viewer along the ground: Load, the viewer's altitude ± NearWindowLayers chunk
	 *   widths up to GetPlanetNearBandCeiling, and nothing for a viewer above it (G52: above the slab the band is air);
	 *   Keep, anything in the shell within the unload distance of the viewer (3D). As a heightmap world's near window
	 *   streams the viewer's layer ± NearWindowLayers within its height bounds: caves and digging below the slab, and the
	 *   chunks around a viewer near it (a flyer near the ground, a pawn at the sea's surface), whose terrain waits need
	 *   them cooked.
	 * Edits off the window are pinned by the chunk manager.
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk coordinates
	 * @param Context Query context (viewer position, world origin)
	 * @param Use Load (stream in) or Keep (retain)
	 * @return True when the chunk is in the window
	 */
	bool IsInPlanetWindow(const FIntVector& ChunkCoord, const FLODQueryContext& Context, EWindowUse Use) const;

	/** A planet chunk's viewer-independent facts (WM-BP8): its radial extent and its slab, as altitudes above the datum. */
	struct FPlanetChunkSlab
	{
		/** Nearest and farthest point of the chunk box from the planet centre, minus PlanetRadius. */
		float AltitudeMin = 0.0f;
		float AltitudeMax = 0.0f;
		/** The surface's altitude range over the cells the chunk's corners span, ± SlabSlackChunks (the whole shell when off). */
		float SlabMin = 0.0f;
		float SlabMax = 0.0f;
	};

	/**
	 * A planet chunk's radial extent and slab, memoized for the strategy's lifetime (the terrain is immutable per world).
	 * The slab is the union of the per-cell surface ranges (GetPlanetCellSurfaceRange) of the cube-sphere cells the
	 * chunk's eight corner directions span (FVoxelCubeSphereGrid::GatherSpanned), widened by SlabSlackChunks. Game thread.
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk coordinates
	 * @return The chunk's altitude extent and slab
	 */
	FPlanetChunkSlab GetPlanetChunkSlab(const FIntVector& ChunkCoord) const;

	/**
	 * One cube-sphere cell's analytic surface altitude range (WM-BP8): GetTerrainAltitude at its four corners and centre,
	 * as a heightmap column's GetSurfaceRange samples five heights. Memoized. Game thread.
	 * @param Cell Atlas coordinate on PlanetSlabGrid
	 * @return Altitude range (uu above the datum)
	 */
	FFloatInterval GetPlanetCellSurfaceRange(const FIntPoint& Cell) const;

	/**
	 * Calls Visit once for every chunk that may be in the planet's window for this viewer (WM-BP8): the chunks crossing the
	 * spherical shell of the window's altitude envelope inside the cone of the load horizon around the viewer's up-line,
	 * plus the near window's cone and envelope (for Load up to GetPlanetNearBandCeiling). A superset: the caller applies
	 * IsInPlanetWindow and the horizon. Columns run along the grid axis closest to the viewer's up, so each crosses the
	 * envelope steeply.
	 * @param Context Query context (viewer position, world origin)
	 * @param Use Load (stream in) or Keep (retain: the near window holds the shell within the unload distance)
	 * @param Visit Called with each candidate's chunk coordinates (no repeats)
	 */
	void ForEachPlanetCandidate(const FLODQueryContext& Context, EWindowUse Use, TFunctionRef<void(const FIntVector&)> Visit) const;

	/** GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope's memo: the direction's cell and the angle it was built for, and the envelope. */
	struct FSurfaceEnvelopeMemo
	{
		FIntPoint Cell = FIntPoint(MIN_int32, MIN_int32);
		double Angle = -1.0;
		FFloatInterval Range;
	};

	/**
	 * The surface's altitude envelope over the disk of cells within an angle of a direction (WM-BP8): the union of their
	 * GetPlanetCellSurfaceRange. Memoized for the last direction cell and angle. Game thread.
	 * @param Direction Unit direction from the planet centre (the viewer's up)
	 * @param Angle Angular radius of the disk (radians), margins included
	 * @param Memo The caller's memo (the load disk's and the near disk's are kept apart, so neither rebuilds the other's)
	 * @return Altitude envelope (uu above the datum), without slack
	 */
	FFloatInterval GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope(const FVector& Direction, double Angle, FSurfaceEnvelopeMemo& Memo) const;

	/**
	 * The chunk layers whose chunks overlap the world-Z interval [Lo, Hi] (touching counts).
	 * @param Lo Interval bottom, world Z
	 * @param Hi Interval top, world Z
	 * @param OriginZ World origin Z (layer 0's bottom)
	 * @param OutMin Lowest such layer
	 * @param OutMax Highest such layer (below OutMin when none)
	 */
	void GetLayersOverlapping(double Lo, double Hi, double OriginZ, int32& OutMin, int32& OutMax) const;

	/**
	 * Find the LOD band containing the given distance.
	 * Returns nullptr if beyond all bands.
	 */
	const FLODBand* FindBandForDistance(float Distance) const;

	/**
	 * Find the band whose LODLevel equals the given level (first match).
	 * Used by hysteresis to look up a committed LOD's distance edges.
	 */
	const FLODBand* FindBandByLOD(int32 LODLevel) const;

	/**
	 * Raw distance-band LOD for a chunk, ignoring balancing/hysteresis.
	 * This is the unmodified band lookup; the public GetLODForChunk layers
	 * the balanced cache on top of it.
	 */
	int32 GetRawLODForDistance(float Distance) const;

	/**
	 * Apply LOD hysteresis to damp churn near band edges.
	 * A single-level change is only accepted once the distance has crossed the
	 * committed band's edge by the applicable hysteresis margin (chunk-widths):
	 * RefineHysteresisFraction (eager) when moving closer, CoarsenHysteresisFraction
	 * (damped) when moving away. Multi-level changes (e.g. a teleport) are accepted
	 * immediately. First-seen chunks (no committed value) take the raw LOD.
	 *
	 * @param CommittedLOD The LOD committed for this chunk last frame
	 * @param RawLOD The raw distance-band LOD this frame
	 * @param Distance Chunk-center distance to viewer
	 * @return The LOD to commit this frame
	 */
	int32 ApplyLODHysteresis(int32 CommittedLOD, int32 RawLOD, float Distance) const;

	/**
	 * Recompute BalancedLODCache for all candidate chunks: raw band LOD, then
	 * hysteresis, then the 2:1 adjacency balance (no face-neighbor differs by more
	 * than MaxNeighborLODDelta). Called from Update() when ShouldRebuildBalancedLODCache says so.
	 */
	void RebuildBalancedLODCache(const FLODQueryContext& Context);

	/**
	 * Whether Update must rebuild the balanced LOD cache (WORLD_MODES_REVIEW_PLAN.md G12). The cache is a
	 * function of the viewer position, the world origin, the configuration and the balance cvars, so a
	 * still viewer would rebuild the same map every tick (1.3-1.9 ms on the demo). It rebuilds when the
	 * viewer enters another chunk or moves BalancedLODCacheMoveThreshold, when the origin or a balance
	 * cvar changes, and after Initialize, SetLODBands or SetViewDistance.
	 * @param Context This tick's query context.
	 * @return True when the cached map no longer matches Context.
	 */
	bool ShouldRebuildBalancedLODCache(const FLODQueryContext& Context) const;

	/**
	 * Check if a chunk is within the view frustum.
	 */
	bool IsChunkInFrustum(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const;

	/**
	 * Calculate load priority for a chunk.
	 * Higher values = higher priority.
	 */
	float CalculatePriority(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const;

	/**
	 * Get color for LOD level (for debug visualization).
	 */
	FColor GetLODDebugColor(int32 LODLevel) const;

	/**
	 * Check if chunk should be culled for Island mode (beyond island boundary): its column does not overlap the
	 * island's footprint (FVoxelWorldBounds::IntersectsBox2D), the same test the map's IsTileInsideWorld and the far
	 * ocean use, so the columns that stream are exactly the ones the far ocean leaves open (WM-E1).
	 * Returns true if chunk should be CULLED (not rendered).
	 */
	bool ShouldCullIslandBoundary(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const;

	/**
	 * Check if chunk should be culled for Spherical Planet mode: wholly inside the shell window's inner radius or outside
	 * its outer one, or past the horizon (GetPlanetHorizonDistance, SP-C2).
	 * Returns true if chunk should be CULLED (not rendered).
	 */
	bool ShouldCullBeyondHorizon(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const;

public:
	/**
	 * How far a planet viewer can see terrain (SP-C2): sqrt(2Rh + h^2) + sqrt(2RH + H^2), the viewer's tangent distance to
	 * the datum sphere plus a peak's, so mountains past the viewer's own horizon still load.
	 * @param PlanetRadius Datum radius R
	 * @param ViewerAltitude Viewer height above the datum h (clamped at 0)
	 * @param MaxTerrainHeight The terrain's highest point above the datum H (the shell's top)
	 * @return Distance (uu) past which no terrain shows
	 */
	static double GetPlanetHorizonDistance(double PlanetRadius, double ViewerAltitude, double MaxTerrainHeight);

protected:

protected:
	// ==================== Configuration State ====================

	/** LOD bands sorted by distance */
	TArray<FLODBand> LODBands;

	/** Master LOD enable flag - when false, all chunks use LOD 0 */
	bool bEnableLOD = true;

	/** Enable smooth LOD transitions via vertex morphing */
	bool bEnableMorphing = true;

	/** Enable view frustum culling for chunk visibility */
	bool bEnableFrustumCulling = true;

	/** Multiplier for unload distance (relative to max LOD band distance) */
	float UnloadDistanceMultiplier = 1.2f;

	// ==================== LOD Adjacency Balance + Hysteresis (P2-B) ====================

	/**
	 * Maximum LOD-level difference permitted between face-adjacent chunks (the 2:1
	 * balance rule). The mesher's single-level Transvoxel transition cells can only
	 * bridge a one-level gap, so larger gaps are refined (coarser chunks pulled
	 * finer) until every adjacency is within this delta. See
	 * Documentation/LOD_SEAM_INVESTIGATION.md (P2-B).
	 */
	int32 MaxNeighborLODDelta = 1;

	/**
	 * Hysteresis deadbands in chunk-width units, applied ASYMMETRICALLY: a small refine
	 * margin (eager — detail appears as you approach) and a larger coarsen margin (damped —
	 * terrain you just left doesn't flicker). The asymmetry gives responsive upgrades
	 * without reintroducing band-edge flip/churn. Read from UVoxelWorldConfiguration in
	 * Initialize; overridable via -VoxelLODRefineHyst / -VoxelLODCoarsenHyst.
	 */
	float RefineHysteresisFraction = 0.25f;
	float CoarsenHysteresisFraction = 0.5f;

	/**
	 * Balanced LOD per chunk, recomputed when the viewer moves (ShouldRebuildBalancedLODCache).
	 * GetLODForChunk and GetVisibleChunks read this so all consumers see the same balanced result.
	 * Empty / missing entries fall back to the raw distance-band LOD.
	 */
	TMap<FIntVector, int32> BalancedLODCache;

	/** LOD committed by the last rebuild per chunk; input to the next rebuild's hysteresis. */
	TMap<FIntVector, int32> CommittedLODCache;

	/** What the last rebuild was computed for; ShouldRebuildBalancedLODCache compares against it. */
	FVector LastRebuildViewerPosition = FVector::ZeroVector;
	FIntVector LastRebuildViewerChunk = FIntVector::ZeroValue;
	FVector LastRebuildWorldOrigin = FVector::ZeroVector;
	int32 LastRebuildBalanceCVar = INDEX_NONE;
	int32 LastRebuildDiagonalCVar = INDEX_NONE;

	/** Set by Initialize, SetLODBands and SetViewDistance: the next Update rebuilds whatever the viewer did. */
	bool bBalancedLODCacheDirty = true;

	/** Rebuilds so far (GetBalancedLODCacheRebuildCount). */
	int32 BalancedLODCacheRebuildCount = 0;

	/** Cached voxel size from configuration */
	float VoxelSize = 100.0f;

	/** Cached base chunk size from configuration */
	int32 BaseChunkSize = 32;

	/** Cached world mode from configuration */
	EWorldMode WorldMode = EWorldMode::InfinitePlane;

	/** Maximum view distance for chunk loading (from Configuration->ViewDistance) */
	float MaxViewDistance = 0.0f;

	/** See GetNearWindowRadius. Set in Initialize from the first LOD band; 0 without bands. */
	float NearWindowRadius = 0.0f;

	// ==================== Heightmap Terrain Bounds ====================

	/**
	 * The configured world mode, built by FVoxelWorldModeFactory (the builder generation uses). The terrain height
	 * bounds and the far-band slab's per-column height come from it, so the culls sample the height the world actually
	 * generates (WM-A3), continentalness included. Immutable after Initialize.
	 */
	TSharedPtr<IVoxelWorldMode> TerrainWorldMode;

	/** Minimum terrain height (SeaLevel + BaseHeight - buffer) */
	float TerrainMinHeight = 0.0f;

	/** Maximum terrain height (SeaLevel + BaseHeight + HeightScale + buffer) */
	float TerrainMaxHeight = 0.0f;

	// ==================== Surface Slab (heightmap worlds) ====================

	/**
	 * When enabled (config bFarBandSurfaceSlabCulling, heightmap worlds), every column streams the chunks around its OWN
	 * surface (± SlabSlackChunks, up to the water plane) at every distance, plus the viewer's layer ± NearWindowLayers
	 * near the viewer (D8, WM-S1). The global height range loads 8 layers per column everywhere (demo geometry), which
	 * is what makes long view distances explode; cave interiors and edits deeper than the slab load only near the viewer
	 * (edits are also pinned by the chunk manager). Off: every column streams the whole height range.
	 */
	bool bSurfaceSlabCulling = false;

	/**
	 * Slab slack in chunk widths: covers surface variation between the 5 footprint samples, POI flatten deltas from the
	 * natural height and the meshing skirt, while keeping the per-column cost at 4-5 layers instead of the height
	 * range's 8 (demo geometry).
	 */
	static constexpr float SlabSlackChunks = 1.5f;

	/** Noise params for the per-column analytic surface sample (TerrainWorldMode->GetSurfaceRange). */
	FVoxelNoiseParams SlabNoiseParams;

	/** Water plane: underwater columns extend their slab up to the water surface (the far ocean
	 *  must keep the chunks that mesh its surface, not just its floor). */
	bool bSlabHasWater = false;
	float SlabWaterLevel = 0.0f;

	/**
	 * Column (chunk XY) -> [min, max] analytic surface height over the chunk footprint
	 * (5-point sample: corners + centre). Memoized for the strategy's lifetime — generation
	 * params are immutable per world. Game-thread only.
	 */
	mutable TMap<FIntPoint, FFloatInterval> ColumnSurfaceCache;

	/** The memoized per-column surface range (world Z) over the chunk footprint. */
	void GetColumnSurfaceRange(int32 ChunkX, int32 ChunkY, const FVector& WorldOrigin,
		float& OutMin, float& OutMax) const;

	// ==================== Island Mode Culling ====================
	// Cached from FVoxelWorldModeFactory::MakeIslandParams, the params generation uses (WM-A1).

	/** Island shape type: 0 = Circular, 1 = Rectangle */
	int32 IslandShape = 0;

	/** Total island extent X (IslandRadius + FalloffWidth) for boundary culling */
	float IslandTotalExtentX = 0.0f;

	/** Total island extent Y (IslandSizeY + FalloffWidth) for rectangle culling */
	float IslandTotalExtentY = 0.0f;

	/** Island centre in world space: WorldOrigin + the config's IslandCenterX/Y, where generation puts it */
	FVector2D IslandCenter = FVector2D::ZeroVector;

	/** The island's footprint (IVoxelWorldMode::GetWorldBounds): a column streams only when it overlaps it */
	FVoxelWorldBounds IslandBounds;

	// ==================== Spherical Planet Mode Culling ====================
	// Cached from FVoxelWorldModeFactory::MakePlanetParams (SP-A6).

	/** Cached planet radius for horizon calculations (double: it meets R-sized distances, WM-BP4) */
	double PlanetRadius = 0.0;

	/**
	 * The terrain's highest point above the datum (the horizon's peaks, SP-C2): its real bounds, the displacement bounds
	 * (FSphericalPlanetWorldMode::GetDisplacementBounds) within the configured shell (WM-BP8).
	 */
	float PlanetMaxTerrainHeight = 0.0f;

	/** The terrain's deepest point below the datum (inner shell culling), from the same real bounds. */
	float PlanetMaxTerrainDepth = 0.0f;

	/** Planet centre in world space (WorldOrigin) */
	FVector PlanetCenter = FVector::ZeroVector;

	/**
	 * The shell window's radii (SP-C1): the terrain's real bounds (WM-BP8: the displacement bounds within the configured
	 * PlanetMaxTerrainHeight / Depth) widened by ShellSlackChunks on both sides.
	 */
	double ShellWindowInnerRadius = 0.0;
	double ShellWindowOuterRadius = 0.0;

	/**
	 * Slack around the terrain shell in chunk widths: a chunk this close to the shell loads, so a seam job beside a peak
	 * or valley at the shell's edge has its neighbour's voxels.
	 */
	static constexpr double ShellSlackChunks = 0.5;

	/** The planet's world mode (TerrainWorldMode, when a planet): the analytic surface the slab and the ground point read. */
	const FSphericalPlanetWorldMode* PlanetWorldMode = nullptr;

	/**
	 * Per-chunk radial slab on a planet (WM-BP8): bFarBandSurfaceSlabCulling on a planet. Off, every chunk in the shell
	 * near the viewer streams (the whole shell inside the horizon's cone).
	 */
	bool bPlanetSlab = false;

	/** The cells the slab caches surface ranges for: about one chunk width across on the datum sphere. */
	FVoxelCubeSphereGrid PlanetSlabGrid;

	/** Cell -> surface altitude range (GetPlanetCellSurfaceRange). Game thread; reset past PlanetSlabCacheLimit entries. */
	mutable TMap<FIntPoint, FFloatInterval> PlanetCellSurfaceCache;

	/** Chunk -> radial extent and slab (GetPlanetChunkSlab). Game thread; reset past PlanetSlabCacheLimit entries. */
	mutable TMap<FIntVector, FPlanetChunkSlab> PlanetChunkSlabCache;

	/** A long flight keeps adding cells and chunks; past this many entries a cache starts over (about 20-30 MB each). */
	static constexpr int32 PlanetSlabCacheLimit = 1000000;

	/** GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope's memos: the load disk's (ForEachPlanetCandidate) and the near disk's (GetPlanetNearBandCeiling). */
	mutable FSurfaceEnvelopeMemo LoadEnvelopeMemo;
	mutable FSurfaceEnvelopeMemo NearEnvelopeMemo;

	/**
	 * The near disk's angular radius for GetPlanetNearBandCeiling: GetNearWindowRadius along the ground at the shell's inner
	 * radius (the lowest ground point, so the widest angle any viewer's near disk subtends), plus the angle half a chunk's
	 * diagonal subtends there (a near chunk's slab reads the cells its corners span). Set in Initialize.
	 */
	double PlanetNearBandAngle = 0.0;

	/** The viewer's ground point (GetPlanetGroundRadius), for the position the last Update saw. */
	FVector GroundRadiusViewer = FVector(TNumericLimits<double>::Max());
	double GroundRadiusCached = 0.0;

	/** The configuration's cut-over altitude (PlanetVoxelCutoverAltitude, else DefaultCutoverViewDistances view distances); 0 off a planet. */
	double PlanetCutoverConfigured = 0.0;

	/** The sea's radius (0 without a sea): the cut-over is measured over the sea where it lies above the terrain. */
	double PlanetSeaRadius = 0.0;

	/** The cut-over state (IsWindowSuspended) and the altitude it was decided at (GetViewerSurfaceAltitude). */
	bool bPlanetWindowSuspended = false;
	double ViewerSurfaceAltitude = 0.0;

	/** The camera's altitude over the same surface (the viewer's plus the context's ViewerLead), and whether it held a resume (G49). */
	double CameraSurfaceAltitude = 0.0;
	bool bCutoverResumeHeld = false;

	/**
	 * The cut-over applies while the chunk manager has a far field (the last Update's context; WM-MP2, D38, every mode
	 * since G78). Heightmap worlds: the sea's world Z (lowest double without a sea); the generated ground Z under the viewer the last Update sampled
	 */
	bool bCutoverAllowed = false;
	double HeightmapSeaZ = TNumericLimits<double>::Lowest();
	FVector HeightmapGroundViewer = FVector(TNumericLimits<double>::Max());
	double HeightmapGroundZ = 0.0;

	// ==================== Runtime State ====================

	/** Cached viewer position from last update */
	FVector CachedViewerPosition = FVector::ZeroVector;

	/** Cached viewer chunk coordinate */
	FIntVector CachedViewerChunk = FIntVector::ZeroValue;

	/** Cached world origin from last update */
	FVector CachedWorldOrigin = FVector::ZeroVector;

	/** Whether the strategy has been initialized */
	bool bIsInitialized = false;
};
```

### Source/VoxelLOD/Public/IVoxelLODStrategy.h
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "LODTypes.h"

// Forward declarations
class UWorld;
class UVoxelWorldConfiguration;

/**
 * LOD Strategy Interface for voxel terrain.
 *
 * All LOD implementations must conform to this interface. Strategies determine
 * which chunks should be loaded/rendered at what detail level based on
 * viewer position and world state.
 *
 * Performance: GetLODForChunk() is called frequently and must be fast (< 1us).
 * Thread Safety: All const methods must be thread-safe for read operations.
 *
 * Implementations:
 * - FDistanceBandLODStrategy (default) - Distance-based LOD rings
 * - FQuadtreeLODStrategy (future) - Screen-space adaptive for 2D terrain
 * - FOctreeLODStrategy (future) - 3D adaptive for spherical/cave systems
 *
 * @see FDistanceBandLODStrategy
 * @see Documentation/LOD_SYSTEM.md
 */
class VOXELLOD_API IVoxelLODStrategy
{
public:
	virtual ~IVoxelLODStrategy() = default;

	// ==================== Core Queries ====================

	/**
	 * Get LOD level for a chunk at given coordinate.
	 *
	 * Called frequently (per chunk per frame). Must be fast and thread-safe.
	 *
	 * Performance: < 1us per call
	 * Thread Safety: Must be thread-safe (const, no mutations)
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk position in chunk coordinate space
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 * @return LOD level (0 = finest detail, higher = coarser)
	 */
	virtual int32 GetLODForChunk(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const = 0;

	/**
	 * Get the LOD level of the distance band a chunk falls in, even when the LOD system is off.
	 *
	 * With LOD off every chunk renders at LOD 0, but the bands still describe distance. Systems
	 * that key on how far a chunk is rather than how coarse it is (far-chunk compression) use this
	 * so they keep working on LOD-off worlds, which includes every cubic world.
	 *
	 * Default: GetLODForChunk (a strategy without a LOD-off mode has nothing to add).
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk position in chunk coordinate space
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 * @return LOD level of the chunk's distance band (0 = nearest band)
	 */
	virtual int32 GetDistanceBandLOD(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const
	{
		return GetLODForChunk(ChunkCoord, Context);
	}

	/**
	 * Get morph factor for LOD transition blending.
	 *
	 * Used to smoothly blend between LOD levels in the vertex shader.
	 * Returns 0 when fully at current LOD, 1 when ready to transition to next.
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk position in chunk coordinate space
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 * @return Morph factor 0-1 (0 = current LOD, 1 = next LOD)
	 */
	virtual float GetLODMorphFactor(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const = 0;

	// ==================== Visibility & Streaming ====================

	/**
	 * Get all chunks that should be visible this frame.
	 *
	 * Returns the complete set of chunks that need to be rendered,
	 * sorted by priority (highest first).
	 *
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 * @return Array of chunk requests with LOD and priority
	 */
	virtual TArray<FChunkLODRequest> GetVisibleChunks(
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const = 0;

	/**
	 * Get chunks that need to be loaded (not currently loaded).
	 *
	 * Called by ChunkManager to determine what to generate/mesh.
	 * Should respect MaxChunksToLoadPerFrame from context.
	 *
	 * @param OutLoad Output array of chunks to load (sorted by priority)
	 * @param LoadedChunks Set of currently loaded chunk coordinates
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 */
	virtual void GetChunksToLoad(
		TArray<FChunkLODRequest>& OutLoad,
		const TSet<FIntVector>& LoadedChunks,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const = 0;

	/**
	 * Get every chunk that is out of range and may be unloaded, farthest first.
	 *
	 * Called by ChunkManager to free memory from distant chunks. Return ALL candidates and do NOT
	 * apply MaxChunksToUnloadPerFrame here: the caller first drops candidates it must keep (chunks
	 * still in the generation/meshing pipeline, edit-pinned chunks) and only then applies the
	 * per-frame cap (see SelectUnloadCandidates). A strategy-side cap let refused candidates use up
	 * the budget; because the loaded set iterates in a stable order, a handful of them could stop
	 * every later chunk from ever unloading (VOXEL_QA_FOLLOWUPS_PLAN.md R23d).
	 *
	 * @param OutUnload Output array of chunk coordinates to unload, sorted farthest first
	 * @param LoadedChunks Set of currently loaded chunk coordinates
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 */
	virtual void GetChunksToUnload(
		TArray<FIntVector>& OutUnload,
		const TSet<FIntVector>& LoadedChunks,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const = 0;

	/**
	 * Pick this frame's unloads from a candidate list (as returned by GetChunksToUnload).
	 *
	 * Candidates the caller refuses are skipped WITHOUT spending budget; selection stops once
	 * MaxPerFrame candidates have been accepted. Candidate order is kept, so a farthest-first
	 * list stays farthest first.
	 *
	 * Performance: O(n) in the number of candidates, one CanUnload call each until the cap.
	 *
	 * @param Candidates  Unload candidates in priority order (farthest first).
	 * @param CanUnload   Caller veto: return false to keep a candidate resident this frame.
	 * @param MaxPerFrame Cap on accepted candidates (<= 0 = no cap).
	 * @param OutSelected Receives the accepted candidates (reset first).
	 * @return Number of candidates selected.
	 */
	static int32 SelectUnloadCandidates(
		const TArray<FIntVector>& Candidates,
		TFunctionRef<bool(const FIntVector&)> CanUnload,
		int32 MaxPerFrame,
		TArray<FIntVector>& OutSelected)
	{
		OutSelected.Reset();
		for (const FIntVector& Coord : Candidates)
		{
			if (MaxPerFrame > 0 && OutSelected.Num() >= MaxPerFrame)
			{
				break;
			}
			if (CanUnload(Coord))
			{
				OutSelected.Add(Coord);
			}
		}
		return OutSelected.Num();
	}

	// ==================== Lifecycle ====================

	/**
	 * Initialize strategy from world configuration.
	 *
	 * Called once when the voxel world is created. Use this to
	 * cache configuration values and pre-compute any needed data.
	 *
	 * @param WorldConfig World configuration asset
	 */
	virtual void Initialize(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration* WorldConfig) = 0;

	/**
	 * Update strategy state each frame.
	 *
	 * Called every frame from game thread before any LOD queries.
	 * Use for temporal logic, hysteresis, or state updates.
	 *
	 * @param Context Query context with viewer and world state
	 * @param DeltaTime Time since last update in seconds
	 */
	virtual void Update(const FLODQueryContext& Context, float DeltaTime) = 0;

	// ==================== Optional Optimization ====================

	/**
	 * Should this chunk be updated this frame?
	 *
	 * Optional throttling mechanism. Return false to skip expensive
	 * updates for chunks that haven't changed significantly.
	 *
	 * Default: Always returns true
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk position
	 * @param Context Query context
	 * @return True if chunk should be updated
	 */
	virtual bool ShouldUpdateChunk(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const
	{
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Get priority for chunk generation/loading.
	 *
	 * Higher priority chunks are processed first. Used for sorting
	 * the generation queue.
	 *
	 * Default: Returns inverse distance (closer = higher priority)
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCoord Chunk position
	 * @param Context Query context
	 * @return Priority value (higher = more important)
	 */
	virtual float GetChunkPriority(
		const FIntVector& ChunkCoord,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const
	{
		return 1.0f;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the distance (world units) beyond which a loaded chunk is out of range and
	 * should be unloaded. Also used to cull chunks from the generation/mesh queue before
	 * they ever load, when the viewer has moved far past them while they sat in the backlog.
	 *
	 * Default: -1 (no unload horizon -> stale-culling disabled for this strategy).
	 *
	 * @return Unload horizon distance in world units, or <= 0 to disable.
	 */
	virtual float GetUnloadDistance() const
	{
		return -1.0f;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the load horizon (world units): the distance within which the strategy streams chunks in
	 * (the view edge). Smaller than GetUnloadDistance(), whose margin is hysteresis, not view range.
	 * The chunk manager pin-loads chunks that exist only because of edits within this radius, so an
	 * edited chunk never appears on its own beyond the rest of the terrain, and keeps them resident
	 * out to GetUnloadDistance().
	 *
	 * Default: -1 (no load horizon; callers fall back to GetUnloadDistance()).
	 *
	 * @return Load horizon distance in world units, or <= 0 when the strategy defines none.
	 */
	virtual float GetLoadDistance() const
	{
		return -1.0f;
	}

	/**
	 * The distance the load and unload horizons (GetLoadDistance, GetUnloadDistance) are measured in, from the viewer
	 * to a chunk's centre. Everything that asks whether a chunk is in range (the strategy's own load and unload, the
	 * chunk manager's queue eviction, edit pins and residency audit) uses it, so they cannot disagree (KI11).
	 *
	 * Default: 3D distance. FDistanceBandLODStrategy: horizontal distance in heightmap worlds, whose vertical extent is
	 * each column's own window (world modes review D8), so the viewer's altitude never removes the ground under it; on a
	 * planet the distance along the ground from the viewer's ground point, each chunk's radial extent being its slab
	 * (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP8).
	 *
	 * @param ChunkCenter Chunk centre, world space
	 * @param ViewerPosition Viewer position, world space
	 * @return Distance compared against the horizons, world units
	 */
	virtual float GetHorizonDistance(const FVector& ChunkCenter, const FVector& ViewerPosition) const
	{
		return static_cast<float>(FVector::Dist(ChunkCenter, ViewerPosition));
	}

	/**
	 * Whether the window is empty because the viewer is too high for voxels to matter (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP10, D18: a
	 * planet's viewer above its voxel cut-over altitude, where the far field alone draws the planet). While it is,
	 * GetVisibleChunks returns nothing and GetChunksToUnload every loaded chunk, and the chunk manager neither pins edited
	 * chunks nor keeps queued ones. Set by Update.
	 *
	 * Default: false (the window never empties).
	 *
	 * @return True while the window is suspended
	 */
	virtual bool IsWindowSuspended() const
	{
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * The altitude over the surface under the viewer above which the window suspends (IsWindowSuspended), and the
	 * viewer's altitude over that surface as the last Update saw it (spherical Phase 6, WM-BP10).
	 *
	 * Default: 0 (never) and 0.
	 */
	virtual double GetCutoverAltitude() const
	{
		return 0.0;
	}

	/**
	 * Whether the chunk manager has a far field to draw the world beyond the window: the cut-over is in force only
	 * while it has (D38; every mode since G78). The chunk manager sets it when the far field is built or released and
	 * every Update's context carries it (FLODQueryContext::bFarFieldActive), so GetCutoverAltitude is right before the
	 * first Update too. Default: nothing to set.
	 */
	virtual void SetFarFieldActive(bool bActive)
	{
	}
	virtual double GetViewerSurfaceAltitude() const
	{
		return 0.0;
	}

	// ==================== Debugging ====================

	/**
	 * Get debug information string.
	 *
	 * Returns human-readable debug info for on-screen display
	 * and logging. Include strategy name, configuration, and stats.
	 *
	 * @return Debug information string
	 */
	virtual FString GetDebugInfo() const = 0;

	/**
	 * Draw debug visualization in viewport.
	 *
	 * Optional: Draw LOD zones, chunk bounds, priority heat maps, etc.
	 * Only called when debug visualization is enabled.
	 *
	 * @param World World to draw in
	 * @param Context Query context
	 */
	virtual void DrawDebugVisualization(
		UWorld* World,
		const FLODQueryContext& Context
	) const
	{
		// Default: no visualization
	}
};
```

### Source/VoxelMap/Private/VoxelMapEditOverlay.cpp
```
// Copyright Daniel Raquel. All Rights Reserved.

#include "VoxelMapEditOverlay.h"
#include "VoxelSurfaceQuery.h"
#include "Algo/BinarySearch.h"
#include "Serialization/Archive.h"

namespace
{
	/** Largest supported tile edge: column indices are stored as uint16. */
	constexpr int32 MaxOverlayResolution = 256;

	bool IsBorderColumn(int32 Column, int32 Resolution)
	{
		const int32 PX = Column % Resolution;
		const int32 PY = Column / Resolution;
		return PX == 0 || PY == 0 || PX == Resolution - 1 || PY == Resolution - 1;
	}

	/**
	 * Index of the solid voxel under the crossing ExtractSurfaceFromColumn reported. It returns
	 * Height = BaseZ + (i + T) * VoxelSize with T in [0, 1], so floor() lands on i, or on i + 1 when T is 1, or one
	 * below through rounding. Only one of three neighbouring indices can be a solid-under-air crossing.
	 */
	int32 FindCrossingIndex(const TArray<FVoxelData>& Column, float Height, float BaseZ, float VoxelSize)
	{
		const int32 Guess = FMath::Clamp(FMath::FloorToInt((Height - BaseZ) / VoxelSize), 0, Column.Num() - 2);
		for (const int32 Candidate : { Guess, Guess - 1, Guess + 1 })
		{
			if (Candidate >= 0 && Candidate + 1 < Column.Num() && Column[Candidate].IsSolid() && Column[Candidate + 1].IsAir())
			{
				return Candidate;
			}
		}
		return INDEX_NONE;
	}
}

int32 FVoxelMapEditOverlay::FindColumn(int32 PX, int32 PY) const
{
	if (Resolution <= 0 || PX < 0 || PY < 0 || PX >= Resolution || PY >= Resolution)
	{
		return INDEX_NONE;
	}
	return Algo::BinarySearch(Columns, static_cast<uint16>(PY * Resolution + PX));
}

bool FVoxelMapEditOverlay::IsPending(int32 PX, int32 PY) const
{
	if (Resolution <= 0 || PX < 0 || PY < 0 || PX >= Resolution || PY >= Resolution)
	{
		return false;
	}
	return Algo::BinarySearch(PendingColumns, static_cast<uint16>(PY * Resolution + PX)) != INDEX_NONE;
}

FVoxelMapEditOverlay FVoxelMapEditOverlay::Build(
	const FVoxelMapOverlayBuildInput& Input,
	TConstArrayView<float> AnalyticHeights,
	TFunctionRef<uint8(int32 PX, int32 PY)> AnalyticMaterial)
{
	FVoxelMapEditOverlay Out;
	const int32 CS = Input.ChunkSize;
	const float VS = Input.VoxelSize;
	Out.Resolution = CS;
	if (CS <= 1 || CS > MaxOverlayResolution || VS <= 0.0f || AnalyticHeights.Num() != CS * CS)
	{
		return Out;
	}
	const int32 NumColumns = CS * CS;
	const int32 VolumeSize = NumColumns * CS;
	const float ChunkWorldSize = CS * VS;

	// The stack, sorted by Z. Malformed voxel arrays read as not loaded; malformed edit tables as unedited.
	TArray<const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk*> Stack;
	for (const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk& Chunk : Input.Chunks)
	{
		Stack.Add(&Chunk);
	}
	Stack.Sort([](const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk& A, const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk& B) { return A.ChunkZ < B.ChunkZ; });
	auto FindChunk = [&Stack](int32 ChunkZ) -> const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk*
	{
		for (const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk : Stack)
		{
			if (Chunk->ChunkZ == ChunkZ)
			{
				return Chunk;
			}
		}
		return nullptr;
	};
	auto HasVoxels = [VolumeSize](const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk)
	{
		return Chunk && Chunk->Voxels.IsValid() && Chunk->Voxels->Num() == VolumeSize;
	};
	auto TopEditedAt = [NumColumns](const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk, int32 Column) -> int32
	{
		return (Chunk && Chunk->TopEditedZ.Num() == NumColumns) ? Chunk->TopEditedZ[Column] : -1;
	};

	TArray<FVoxelData> Column;
	TArray<bool, TInlineAllocator<16>> ChunkIsReal;

	for (int32 Col = 0; Col < NumColumns; ++Col)
	{
		// The column's edited extent across the stack, as global voxel indices (ChunkZ * CS + local Z).
		int64 TopEdited = MIN_int64;
		int32 MinEditedChunk = MAX_int32;
		int32 MaxEditedChunk = MIN_int32;
		for (const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk : Stack)
		{
			const int32 LocalZ = TopEditedAt(Chunk, Col);
			if (LocalZ >= 0)
			{
				TopEdited = FMath::Max(TopEdited, static_cast<int64>(Chunk->ChunkZ) * CS + LocalZ);
				MinEditedChunk = FMath::Min(MinEditedChunk, Chunk->ChunkZ);
				MaxEditedChunk = FMath::Max(MaxEditedChunk, Chunk->ChunkZ);
			}
		}
		if (TopEdited == MIN_int64)
		{
			continue;
		}

		const int32 PX = Col % CS;
		const int32 PY = Col / CS;
		const float AnalyticHeight = AnalyticHeights[Col];
		const int32 AnalyticChunk = FMath::FloorToInt((AnalyticHeight - Input.WorldOriginZ) / ChunkWorldSize);

		// Scan from one chunk above the highest edited (or analytic surface) chunk, so a build reaching the top of
		// its chunk still has air above it, down to one chunk below the lowest, so a dig through the bottom of the
		// edited range meets the ground under it. Stop above the first chunk this column cannot read: one that is
		// edited here but has no data.
		const int32 TopChunk = FMath::Max(MaxEditedChunk, AnalyticChunk) + 1;
		const int32 BottomChunk = FMath::Min(MinEditedChunk, AnalyticChunk) - 1;
		int32 LowChunk = TopChunk;
		for (int32 ChunkZ = TopChunk; ChunkZ >= BottomChunk; --ChunkZ)
		{
			const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk = FindChunk(ChunkZ);
			if (Chunk && !HasVoxels(Chunk) && TopEditedAt(Chunk, Col) >= 0)
			{
				break;
			}
			LowChunk = ChunkZ;
		}

		// Assemble the column bottom-up. Chunks without data that this column does not edit read as the analytic
		// terrain: a linear density across the analytic height, so the interpolated crossing lands on it.
		const int32 NumChunks = TopChunk - LowChunk + 1;
		Column.SetNumUninitialized(NumChunks * CS);
		ChunkIsReal.SetNumUninitialized(NumChunks);
		for (int32 ChunkIndex = 0; ChunkIndex < NumChunks; ++ChunkIndex)
		{
			const int32 ChunkZ = LowChunk + ChunkIndex;
			const FVoxelMapOverlayChunk* Chunk = FindChunk(ChunkZ);
			const int32 Base = ChunkIndex * CS;
			ChunkIsReal[ChunkIndex] = HasVoxels(Chunk);
			if (ChunkIsReal[ChunkIndex])
			{
				const TArray<FVoxelData>& Voxels = *Chunk->Voxels;
				for (int32 LocalZ = 0; LocalZ < CS; ++LocalZ)
				{
					Column[Base + LocalZ] = Voxels[PX + PY * CS + LocalZ * NumColumns];
				}
			}
			else
			{
				for (int32 LocalZ = 0; LocalZ < CS; ++LocalZ)
				{
					const float Z = Input.WorldOriginZ + (static_cast<float>(ChunkZ) * CS + LocalZ) * VS;
					FVoxelData Voxel = FVoxelData::Air();
					Voxel.Density = static_cast<uint8>(FMath::Clamp(
						FMath::FloorToInt(VOXEL_SURFACE_THRESHOLD + (AnalyticHeight - Z) / VS * 128.0f), 0, 255));
					if (Voxel.IsAir() && Input.bUseWater && Z < Input.WaterLevel)
					{
						Voxel.SetWaterFlag(true);
					}
					Column[Base + LocalZ] = Voxel;
				}
			}
		}

		const float BaseZ = Input.WorldOriginZ + static_cast<float>(LowChunk) * ChunkWorldSize;
		float Height = 0.0f;
		uint8 MaterialID = 0;
		uint8 BiomeID = 0;
		const int32 Crossing = FVoxelSurfaceQuery::ExtractSurfaceFromColumn(Column, BaseZ, VS, Height, MaterialID, BiomeID)
			? FindCrossingIndex(Column, Height, BaseZ, VS)
			: INDEX_NONE;
		if (Crossing == INDEX_NONE)
		{
			// No surface above the first unreadable chunk or the bottom of the stack: dug through.
			Out.PendingColumns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
			continue;
		}

		// Every edit lies below the surface voxel: the top surface is untouched (dungeon interiors, buried rooms).
		if (TopEdited < static_cast<int64>(LowChunk) * CS + Crossing)
		{
			continue;
		}

		if (!ChunkIsReal[Crossing / CS])
		{
			// The surface sits in a chunk read as analytic. That is the real surface when the analytic height lies
			// between this voxel and the next; when the real voxel above is air although the analytic terrain is
			// solid there, an edit opened the column into a chunk that is not loaded.
			const float ZAbove = BaseZ + (Crossing + 1) * VS;
			if (AnalyticHeight >= ZAbove)
			{
				Out.PendingColumns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
			}
			continue;
		}

		// Water: a water-flagged voxel in the air run above the surface. A pit dug into the seabed is water although
		// the voxels it opened are not flagged yet, because the sea above them is; a pit dug on land below the water
		// line has only dry air above it and stays land until water propagation floods it.
		bool bWater = false;
		for (int32 Above = Crossing + 1; Above < Column.Num() && Column[Above].IsAir(); ++Above)
		{
			if (Column[Above].HasWaterFlag())
			{
				bWater = true;
				break;
			}
		}
		const bool bAnalyticWater = Input.bUseWater && AnalyticHeight < Input.WaterLevel;
		if (FMath::Abs(Height - AnalyticHeight) <= 0.5f * VS && bWater == bAnalyticWater
			&& MaterialID == AnalyticMaterial(PX, PY))
		{
			// The edit left the surface as the analytic map already draws it (e.g. a sub-threshold brush).
			continue;
		}

		Out.Columns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
		Out.Heights.Add(Height);
		Out.Materials.Add(MaterialID);
		Out.Flags.Add(bWater ? FlagWater : 0);
	}
	return Out;
}

FVoxelMapEditOverlay FVoxelMapEditOverlay::BuildPlanet(
	const FVoxelMapPlanetOverlayInput& Input,
	TConstArrayView<FVector> PixelDirections,
	TConstArrayView<float> AnalyticAltitudes,
	TFunctionRef<uint8(int32 PX, int32 PY)> AnalyticMaterial)
{
	FVoxelMapEditOverlay Out;
	const int32 CS = Input.ChunkSize;
	const double VS = Input.VoxelSize;
	Out.Resolution = CS;
	Out.bAltitudeHeights = true;
	const int32 NumColumns = CS * CS;
	if (CS <= 1 || CS > MaxOverlayResolution || VS <= 0.0 || PixelDirections.Num() != NumColumns || AnalyticAltitudes.Num() != NumColumns)
	{
		return Out;
	}
	const int32 VolumeSize = NumColumns * CS;
	const double ChunkWorldSize = CS * VS;
	const FVector& Center = Input.Center;
	const double Radius = Input.PlanetRadius;
	const float Iso = static_cast<float>(VOXEL_SURFACE_THRESHOLD);

	// The chunks by coordinate, and the boxes of those with edits (only lines through them can change).
	TMap<FIntVector, const FVoxelMapPlanetOverlayChunk*> ByCoord;
	TArray<FBox, TInlineAllocator<16>> EditedBoxes;
	for (const FVoxelMapPlanetOverlayChunk& Chunk : Input.Chunks)
	{
		ByCoord.Add(Chunk.Coord, &Chunk);
		if (Chunk.EditedVoxels.IsValid() && Chunk.EditedVoxels->Num() == VolumeSize)
		{
			const FVector Min = Input.Origin + FVector(Chunk.Coord) * ChunkWorldSize;
			EditedBoxes.Add(FBox(Min, Min + FVector(ChunkWorldSize)));
		}
	}
	if (EditedBoxes.Num() == 0)
	{
		return Out;
	}

	// Where the line from the centre along D crosses a box: [T0, T1] (slab test).
	auto RayBox = [&Center](const FVector& D, const FBox& Box, double& OutT0, double& OutT1)
	{
		double T0 = 0.0;
		double T1 = TNumericLimits<double>::Max();
		for (int32 Axis = 0; Axis < 3; ++Axis)
		{
			if (FMath::Abs(D[Axis]) < 1.0e-12)
			{
				if (Center[Axis] < Box.Min[Axis] || Center[Axis] > Box.Max[Axis])
				{
					return false;
				}
				continue;
			}
			double A = (Box.Min[Axis] - Center[Axis]) / D[Axis];
			double B = (Box.Max[Axis] - Center[Axis]) / D[Axis];
			if (A > B)
			{
				Swap(A, B);
			}
			T0 = FMath::Max(T0, A);
			T1 = FMath::Min(T1, B);
			if (T0 > T1)
			{
				return false;
			}
		}
		OutT0 = T0;
		OutT1 = T1;
		return true;
	};

	enum class ESource : uint8 { Real, StandIn, Unreadable };

	for (int32 Col = 0; Col < NumColumns; ++Col)
	{
		const FVector D = PixelDirections[Col];
		const float AnalyticAltitude = AnalyticAltitudes[Col];
		const double AnalyticRadius = Radius + AnalyticAltitude;

		double EditMin = TNumericLimits<double>::Max();
		double EditMax = TNumericLimits<double>::Lowest();
		for (const FBox& Box : EditedBoxes)
		{
			double T0 = 0.0, T1 = 0.0;
			if (RayBox(D, Box, T0, T1))
			{
				EditMin = FMath::Min(EditMin, T0);
				EditMax = FMath::Max(EditMax, T1);
			}
		}
		if (EditMin > EditMax)
		{
			continue;
		}

		// The voxel with index I (density sample at Origin + I * VS): from its chunk when listed and loaded; the analytic
		// terrain along this line when the chunk is not listed (solid below the analytic radius, the sea's water flag in
		// the air under the sea radius); unreadable when listed without data (an edited chunk that is not loaded).
		auto Read = [&](const FIntVector& I, FVoxelData& OutVoxel, bool& bOutEdited) -> ESource
		{
			bOutEdited = false;
			const FIntVector ChunkCoord(
				FMath::FloorToInt32(static_cast<double>(I.X) / CS),
				FMath::FloorToInt32(static_cast<double>(I.Y) / CS),
				FMath::FloorToInt32(static_cast<double>(I.Z) / CS));
			if (const FVoxelMapPlanetOverlayChunk* const* Found = ByCoord.Find(ChunkCoord))
			{
				const FVoxelMapPlanetOverlayChunk& Chunk = **Found;
				if (!Chunk.Voxels.IsValid() || Chunk.Voxels->Num() != VolumeSize)
				{
					return ESource::Unreadable;
				}
				const FIntVector Local = I - ChunkCoord * CS;
				const int32 Index = Local.X + Local.Y * CS + Local.Z * NumColumns;
				OutVoxel = (*Chunk.Voxels)[Index];
				bOutEdited = Chunk.EditedVoxels.IsValid() && Chunk.EditedVoxels->Num() == VolumeSize && (*Chunk.EditedVoxels)[Index];
				return ESource::Real;
			}
			const double R = FVector::Dist(Input.Origin + FVector(I) * VS, Center);
			OutVoxel = FVoxelData::Air();
			OutVoxel.Density = static_cast<uint8>(FMath::Clamp(FMath::FloorToInt32(Iso + (AnalyticRadius - R) / VS * 128.0), 0, 255));
			if (OutVoxel.IsAir() && Input.bUseWater && R < Input.WaterRadius)
			{
				OutVoxel.SetWaterFlag(true);
			}
			return ESource::StandIn;
		};

		// Coarse, from the top down: the nearest voxel every half voxel along the line; the first solid voxel under air.
		const double TopT = FMath::Max(AnalyticRadius, EditMax) + 2.0 * VS;
		const double BottomT = FMath::Min(AnalyticRadius, EditMin) - ChunkWorldSize;
		FIntVector Previous(MAX_int32);
		bool bAirAbove = false;
		bool bEditSeen = false;
		bool bWater = false;
		bool bPending = false;
		bool bFound = false;
		bool bSolidAtTop = false;
		double AirT = TopT;
		double SolidT = 0.0;
		FVoxelData Solid;
		ESource SolidSource = ESource::Real;
		for (double T = TopT; T >= BottomT; T -= 0.5 * VS)
		{
			const FVector F = (Center + D * T - Input.Origin) / VS;
			const FIntVector I(FMath::RoundToInt32(F.X), FMath::RoundToInt32(F.Y), FMath::RoundToInt32(F.Z));
			if (I == Previous)
			{
				continue;
			}
			Previous = I;
			FVoxelData Voxel;
			bool bEdited = false;
			const ESource Source = Read(I, Voxel, bEdited);
			if (Source == ESource::Unreadable)
			{
				bPending = true;
				break;
			}
			bEditSeen |= bEdited;
			if (Voxel.IsSolid())
			{
				if (!bAirAbove)
				{
					bSolidAtTop = true;
					break;
				}
				bFound = true;
				SolidT = T;
				Solid = Voxel;
				SolidSource = Source;
				break;
			}
			bWater |= Voxel.HasWaterFlag();
			bAirAbove = true;
			AirT = T;
		}
		if (bSolidAtTop)
		{
			continue;
		}
		if (bPending || !bFound)
		{
			// An edited chunk without data on the way down, or no ground above the bottom of the walk: dug through.
			Out.PendingColumns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
			continue;
		}
		if (!bEditSeen)
		{
			// Every edit on this line lies below the surface (or none is on it): the analytic map already draws it.
			continue;
		}
		if (SolidSource == ESource::StandIn)
		{
			// The surface is the analytic stand-in's: the real one when it sits at the analytic altitude; when real air ran
			// below that, an edit opened the line into a chunk that is not loaded.
			if (AnalyticRadius - SolidT > VS)
			{
				Out.PendingColumns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
			}
			continue;
		}

		// Fine: the trilinear density on the line around the coarse crossing (the nearest voxels stray sideways).
		auto Density = [&](const FIntVector& I) -> float
		{
			FVoxelData Voxel;
			bool bEdited = false;
			if (Read(I, Voxel, bEdited) == ESource::Unreadable)
			{
				const double R = FVector::Dist(Input.Origin + FVector(I) * VS, Center);
				return static_cast<float>(FMath::Clamp(Iso + (AnalyticRadius - R) / VS * 128.0, 0.0, 255.0));
			}
			return static_cast<float>(Voxel.Density);
		};
		auto Trilinear = [&](const FVector& P) -> float
		{
			const FVector F = (P - Input.Origin) / VS;
			const FIntVector I0(FMath::FloorToInt32(F.X), FMath::FloorToInt32(F.Y), FMath::FloorToInt32(F.Z));
			const FVector W = F - FVector(I0);
			float Result = 0.0f;
			for (int32 Corner = 0; Corner < 8; ++Corner)
			{
				const FIntVector O(Corner & 1, (Corner >> 1) & 1, (Corner >> 2) & 1);
				const double Weight = (O.X ? W.X : 1.0 - W.X) * (O.Y ? W.Y : 1.0 - W.Y) * (O.Z ? W.Z : 1.0 - W.Z);
				Result += static_cast<float>(Weight) * Density(I0 + O);
			}
			return Result;
		};
		const double Step = 0.25 * VS;
		double HitT = TNumericLimits<double>::Max();
		float AboveDensity = Trilinear(Center + D * (AirT + VS));
		for (double T = AirT + VS - Step; T >= SolidT - 1.5 * VS && AboveDensity < Iso; T -= Step)
		{
			const float Value = Trilinear(Center + D * T);
			if (Value >= Iso)
			{
				HitT = T + Step * (Value - Iso) / FMath::Max(Value - AboveDensity, KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER);
				break;
			}
			AboveDensity = Value;
		}
		if (HitT == TNumericLimits<double>::Max())
		{
			// The fine walk found no crossing (an edge case of the bracket): between the coarse samples.
			HitT = 0.5 * (AirT + SolidT);
		}

		const float Altitude = static_cast<float>(HitT - Radius);
		const bool bAnalyticWater = Input.bUseWater && AnalyticRadius < Input.WaterRadius;
		const int32 PX = Col % CS;
		const int32 PY = Col / CS;
		if (FMath::Abs(Altitude - AnalyticAltitude) <= 0.5 * VS && bWater == bAnalyticWater
			&& Solid.MaterialID == AnalyticMaterial(PX, PY))
		{
			// The edit left the surface as the analytic map already draws it.
			continue;
		}
		Out.Columns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
		Out.Heights.Add(Altitude);
		Out.Materials.Add(Solid.MaterialID);
		Out.Flags.Add(bWater ? FlagWater : 0);
	}
	return Out;
}

FVoxelMapEditOverlay FVoxelMapEditOverlay::MergePending(const FVoxelMapEditOverlay& Built, const FVoxelMapEditOverlay* Previous)
{
	if (!Previous || Previous->IsEmpty() || Built.PendingColumns.Num() == 0 || Previous->Resolution != Built.Resolution
		|| Previous->bAltitudeHeights != Built.bAltitudeHeights)
	{
		return Built;
	}

	FVoxelMapEditOverlay Out;
	Out.Resolution = Built.Resolution;
	Out.bAltitudeHeights = Built.bAltitudeHeights;
	Out.PendingColumns = Built.PendingColumns;
	const int32 Capacity = Built.Num() + FMath::Min(Previous->Num(), Built.PendingColumns.Num());
	Out.Columns.Reserve(Capacity);
	Out.Heights.Reserve(Capacity);
	Out.Materials.Reserve(Capacity);
	Out.Flags.Reserve(Capacity);

	// Three ascending streams: the fresh columns, the previous columns, the pending columns. A column is never both
	// masked and pending in a build, so taking previous entries only at pending columns cannot duplicate one.
	int32 BuiltIndex = 0;
	int32 PrevIndex = 0;
	int32 PendingIndex = 0;
	auto TakeBuilt = [&]()
	{
		Out.Columns.Add(Built.Columns[BuiltIndex]);
		Out.Heights.Add(Built.Heights[BuiltIndex]);
		Out.Materials.Add(Built.Materials[BuiltIndex]);
		Out.Flags.Add(Built.Flags[BuiltIndex]);
		++BuiltIndex;
	};
	while (PrevIndex < Previous->Num())
	{
		const uint16 PrevColumn = Previous->Columns[PrevIndex];
		while (PendingIndex < Built.PendingColumns.Num() && Built.PendingColumns[PendingIndex] < PrevColumn)
		{
			++PendingIndex;
		}
		if (PendingIndex >= Built.PendingColumns.Num())
		{
			break;
		}
		if (Built.PendingColumns[PendingIndex] == PrevColumn)
		{
			while (BuiltIndex < Built.Num() && Built.Columns[BuiltIndex] < PrevColumn)
			{
				TakeBuilt();
			}
			Out.Columns.Add(PrevColumn);
			Out.Heights.Add(Previous->Heights[PrevIndex]);
			Out.Materials.Add(Previous->Materials[PrevIndex]);
			Out.Flags.Add(Previous->Flags[PrevIndex]);
		}
		++PrevIndex;
	}
	while (BuiltIndex < Built.Num())
	{
		TakeBuilt();
	}
	return Out;
}

bool FVoxelMapEditOverlay::BordersEqual(const FVoxelMapEditOverlay* A, const FVoxelMapEditOverlay* B)
{
	static const FVoxelMapEditOverlay Empty;
	const FVoxelMapEditOverlay& L = A ? *A : Empty;
	const FVoxelMapEditOverlay& R = B ? *B : Empty;

	// Walk both in column order, comparing only border entries.
	int32 LI = 0;
	int32 RI = 0;
	while (true)
	{
		while (LI < L.Num() && !IsBorderColumn(L.Columns[LI], L.Resolution))
		{
			++LI;
		}
		while (RI < R.Num() && !IsBorderColumn(R.Columns[RI], R.Resolution))
		{
			++RI;
		}
		const bool bLeftDone = LI >= L.Num();
		const bool bRightDone = RI >= R.Num();
		if (bLeftDone || bRightDone)
		{
			return bLeftDone && bRightDone;
		}
		if (L.Resolution != R.Resolution || L.bAltitudeHeights != R.bAltitudeHeights || L.Columns[LI] != R.Columns[RI] || L.Heights[LI] != R.Heights[RI]
			|| L.Materials[LI] != R.Materials[RI] || L.Flags[LI] != R.Flags[RI])
		{
			return false;
		}
		++LI;
		++RI;
	}
}

bool FVoxelMapEditOverlay::Serialize(FArchive& Ar)
{
	uint8 Version = bAltitudeHeights ? PlanetFormatVersion : FormatVersion;
	Ar << Version;
	uint16 SavedResolution = static_cast<uint16>(Resolution);
	Ar << SavedResolution;

	if (Ar.IsLoading())
	{
		auto Fail = [this]()
		{
			*this = FVoxelMapEditOverlay();
			return false;
		};
		if (Ar.IsError() || (Version != FormatVersion && Version != PlanetFormatVersion) || SavedResolution < 2
			|| SavedResolution > MaxOverlayResolution)
		{
			return Fail();
		}
		Resolution = SavedResolution;
		bAltitudeHeights = Version == PlanetFormatVersion;
		const int32 NumColumns = Resolution * Resolution;
		TArray<uint8> Mask;
		Mask.SetNumZeroed((NumColumns + 7) / 8);
		Ar.Serialize(Mask.GetData(), Mask.Num());
		if (Ar.IsError())
		{
			return Fail();
		}

		Columns.Reset();
		PendingColumns.Reset();
		for (int32 Col = 0; Col < NumColumns; ++Col)
		{
			if (Mask[Col >> 3] & (1 << (Col & 7)))
			{
				Columns.Add(static_cast<uint16>(Col));
			}
		}
		const int32 Count = Columns.Num();
		Heights.SetNumUninitialized(Count);
		Materials.SetNumUninitialized(Count);
		Flags.SetNumUninitialized(Count);
		for (int32 i = 0; i < Count && !Ar.IsError(); ++i)
		{
			Ar << Heights[i];
		}
		if (Count > 0)
		{
			Ar.Serialize(Materials.GetData(), Count);
			Ar.Serialize(Flags.GetData(), Count);
		}
		if (Ar.IsError())
		{
			return Fail();
		}
		return true;
	}

	// Saving: the mask, then the values in column order.
	const int32 NumColumns = Resolution * Resolution;
	TArray<uint8> Mask;
	Mask.SetNumZeroed((NumColumns + 7) / 8);
	for (const uint16 Col : Columns)
	{
		Mask[Col >> 3] |= static_cast<uint8>(1 << (Col & 7));
	}
	Ar.Serialize(Mask.GetData(), Mask.Num());
	for (float& Height : Heights)
	{
		Ar << Height;
	}
	if (Columns.Num() > 0)
	{
		Ar.Serialize(Materials.GetData(), Materials.Num());
		Ar.Serialize(Flags.GetData(), Flags.Num());
	}
	return !Ar.IsError();
}

bool FVoxelMapEditOverlay::operator==(const FVoxelMapEditOverlay& Other) const
{
	return Resolution == Other.Resolution && bAltitudeHeights == Other.bAltitudeHeights && Columns == Other.Columns
		&& Heights == Other.Heights
		&& Materials == Other.Materials && Flags == Other.Flags;
}

	/** The PIE / Game world a console command should act on. */
	UWorld* FindPlayWorld(UWorld* World)
	{
		if (World && (World->WorldType == EWorldType::PIE || World->WorldType == EWorldType::Game))
		{
			return World;
		}
		if (GEngine)
		{
			for (const FWorldContext& Ctx : GEngine->GetWorldContexts())
			{
				if (Ctx.World() && (Ctx.WorldType == EWorldType::PIE || Ctx.WorldType == EWorldType::Game))
				{
					return Ctx.World();
				}
			}
		}
		return nullptr;
	}

	FAutoConsoleCommandWithWorldAndArgs GVoxelMapRedrawCmd(
		TEXT("voxel.Map.Redraw"),
		TEXT("Redraw every explored map tile (current images stay until the new ones land). voxel.Map.Redraw 1 also ")
		TEXT("rebuilds the edit overlay of every edited tile from loaded chunks."),
		FConsoleCommandWithWorldAndArgsDelegate::CreateLambda([](const TArray<FString>& Args, UWorld* World)
		{
			UWorld* Target = FindPlayWorld(World);
			UVoxelMapSubsystem* Map = Target ? Target->GetSubsystem<UVoxelMapSubsystem>() : nullptr;
			if (!Map)
			{
				UE_LOG(LogVoxelMap, Warning, TEXT("voxel.Map.Redraw: no PIE/Game world with a map subsystem (start PIE first)"));
				return;
			}
			Map->RedrawAllTiles(Args.Num() > 0 && FCString::Atoi(*Args[0]) != 0);
		}));

			{

				return;
			}
			const int32 Radius = Args.Num() > 0 ? FCString::Atoi(*Args[0]) : 6;
			const FString Name = Args.Num() > 1 ? Args[1] : FDateTime::Now().ToString(TEXT("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"));
			const bool bHighlight = Args.Num() > 2 && FCString::Atoi(*Args[2]) != 0;

				? FVector(FCString::Atod(*Args[3]), FCString::Atod(*Args[4]), 0.0)

			UE_LOG(LogVoxelMap, Log, TEXT("voxel.Map.Capture: %s %s (radius %d, centre %s, pawn %s)"),
				bOk ? TEXT("wrote") : TEXT("FAILED to write"), *Path, Radius, *Centre.ToCompactString(),
				*Pawn->GetActorLocation().ToCompactString());
		}));

	/**
	 * A standalone analytic world mode for the configuration, from the factory every world-mode consumer uses
	 * (FVoxelWorldModeFactory, WM-A1), so the map's island and planet match generation.
	 *
	 * The map subsystem owns its OWN instance instead of borrowing the chunk manager's: background
	 * tile tasks capture it by TSharedPtr, and the chunk manager destroys its instance in
	 * EndPlay->Shutdown() while tile tasks can still be running — the PIE-stop use-after-free.
	 *
	 * The factory sets the biome context: world modes snapshot the biome config BY VALUE
	 * (FVoxelBiomeSnapshot — plain data, no UObject reference), so the instance stays safe for tasks
	 * that outlive the world's GC purge while GetTerrainHeightAt returns the TRUE generated surface
	 * height (continentalness offset AND height-scale modulation, composed correctly per mode; see
	 * Documentation/Research/MAP_ACCURACY_PLAN.md).
	 */
	TSharedPtr<const IVoxelWorldMode> CreateStandaloneWorldMode(const UVoxelWorldConfiguration& Config)
	{
		return FVoxelWorldModeFactory::Create(Config);
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Key packing (FIntPoint -> uint64)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

uint64 UVoxelMapSubsystem::PackTileKey(FIntPoint Coord)
{
	return (static_cast<uint64>(static_cast<uint32>(Coord.X)) << 32) | static_cast<uint64>(static_cast<uint32>(Coord.Y));
}

FIntPoint UVoxelMapSubsystem::UnpackTileKey(uint64 Key)
{
	return FIntPoint(
		static_cast<int32>(static_cast<uint32>(Key >> 32)),
		static_cast<int32>(static_cast<uint32>(Key & 0xFFFFFFFF))
	);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Lifecycle
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

bool UVoxelMapSubsystem::ShouldCreateSubsystem(UObject* Outer) const
{
	// Only create in game worlds (PIE + standalone), not editor preview
	if (const UWorld* World = Cast<UWorld>(Outer))
	{
		return World->IsGameWorld();
	}
	return false;
}

void UVoxelMapSubsystem::Initialize(FSubsystemCollectionBase& Collection)
{
	Super::Initialize(Collection);
	UE_LOG(LogVoxelMap, Log, TEXT("UVoxelMapSubsystem initialized"));

	// Attempt to resolve chunk manager immediately.
	// It may not be available yet (depends on actor initialization order),
	// so we also resolve lazily in RequestTilesInRadius / OnChunkGenerated.
	ResolveChunkManager();
}

void UVoxelMapSubsystem::Deinitialize()
{
	// Block new task launches and mark in-flight completions for discard before anything else.
	bShuttingDown = true;

	// Unbind delegates
	if (bDelegatesBound && CachedChunkManagerWeak.IsValid())
	{
		CachedChunkManagerWeak->OnChunkGenerated.RemoveDynamic(this, &UVoxelMapSubsystem::OnChunkGenerated);
		CachedChunkManagerWeak->OnTerrainConditioningChanged.Remove(ConditioningChangedHandle);
		ConditioningChangedHandle.Reset();
		bDelegatesBound = false;
	}
	if (UVoxelEditManager* EditManager = CachedEditManagerWeak.Get())
	{
		EditManager->OnChunkEdited.Remove(ChunkEditedHandle);
	}
	ChunkEditedHandle.Reset();
	if (UWorld* World = GetWorld())
	{
		World->GetTimerManager().ClearTimer(OverlayRefreshTimer);
	}

	const int32 InFlight = TileQueue.NumDrawing();
	if (InFlight > 0)
	{
		// In-flight background tasks own their world mode (TSharedPtr capture) and every other input
		// by value, so they finish safely after this point; their game-thread completions see
		// bShuttingDown and discard.
		UE_LOG(LogVoxelMap, Log, TEXT("UVoxelMapSubsystem deinitializing with %d async tile task(s) in flight — completions will be discarded"),
			InFlight);
	}

	// Drop our reference to the standalone world mode; any running task holds its own.
	CachedWorldMode.Reset();
	CachedWorldBounds = FVoxelWorldBounds();

	TileStore.Reset();
	ExploredTiles.Empty();
	DetailWanted.Empty();
	TileQueue.Reset();
	EditOverlays.Empty();
	TileEditedChunkZ.Empty();
	OverlayDirtyTiles.Empty();
	OverlayAwaitingTiles.Empty();
	OverlayRebuildTiles.Empty();
	TileAnalyticRange.Empty();
	PlanetTileEditedChunks.Empty();
